item.content:encoded:
Organizations using sport and physical activity to tackle gender-based violence, discrimination, exclusion and harmful gender norms can apply for The Next Move, a multi-year general support funding opportunity under the United by Sport program. The initiative is designed to strengthen organizations that use sport as a vehicle for social impact and help create safer, more inclusive and cohesive communities.

Selected organizations can receive €150,000, €200,000 or €250,000 over three years, with the funding divided equally across the 36-month partnership. The total funding pool is €2 million.

The opportunity is particularly relevant for nonprofit and grassroots organizations working directly with communities through sport, including organizations addressing gender equality, gender-based violence prevention, inclusion, leadership opportunities for girls and young women, and positive gender norms.

The Next Move Grant 2026

The Next Move is part of the United by Sport program and focuses on supporting organizations that use sport intentionally to address barriers to social cohesion.

The program recognizes that sport can sometimes reproduce existing inequalities, but it can also serve as a powerful platform for positive social change. Through sport and physical activity, organizations can help people build trust, develop positive relationships, challenge discriminatory attitudes and behaviors, and strengthen their sense of belonging.

The funding opportunity specifically focuses on communities in:

  • Brazil
  • Colombia
  • Argentina

Organizations must apply based on one country of implementation, meaning applicants cannot submit a single multi-country application covering several countries.

What Is the Purpose of The Next Move?

The Next Move aims to strengthen organizations that are working to create communities where people feel:

  • Safe
  • Valued
  • Connected
  • Included
  • Able to participate meaningfully
  • Treated fairly and equitably

The program identifies several issues that can prevent people from fully participating in sport and community life. These include gender-based violence, discrimination, exclusion, unequal opportunities and harmful gender norms.

Through general support funding, the adidas Foundation intends to provide organizations with the flexibility to strengthen their overall work rather than requiring them to implement one narrowly defined project.

This means selected organizations can identify their own organizational priorities and determine how the funding can best support their charitable mission, programs and organizational development within the funding guidelines.

Key Focus Areas

The Next Move is particularly interested in organizations working on issues connected to gender, inclusion and social cohesion through sport.

1. Gender-Based Discrimination and Sexism

Organizations may work to address:

  • Gender stereotypes
  • Sexism
  • Unequal opportunities
  • Discriminatory attitudes
  • Exclusion from participation
  • Barriers affecting girls and women in sport

The objective is to help create environments where people can participate in sport and community life without facing discrimination based on gender.

2. Gender-Based Violence

The program also focuses on preventing and addressing gender-based violence, including:

  • Sexual harassment
  • Abuse
  • Intimate partner violence
  • Unsafe environments
  • Other forms of gender-based violence

Sport can be used as a platform to promote safety, awareness, respectful relationships and non-violent behaviors.

3. Inclusion and Equal Participation

Organizations can also contribute by creating opportunities for groups that experience exclusion or unequal access to sport.

This may include initiatives that increase participation, representation and opportunities for girls, young women and non-binary young people.

4. Positive Gender Norms and Masculinities

The Next Move seeks to support organizations promoting healthy, respectful and non-violent gender norms.

This can include work that challenges harmful expectations surrounding gender and encourages healthier relationships and behaviors.

5. Community Connection and Social Cohesion

Sport can bring people together and create opportunities for communities to build trust and stronger relationships.

Organizations may therefore use sport to promote:

  • Belonging
  • Trust
  • Positive relationships
  • Community participation
  • Cooperation
  • Social cohesion

How Much Funding Is Available?

The Next Move offers three possible grant amounts:

  • €150,000
  • €200,000
  • €250,000

The selected amount is provided over three years, meaning the grant is divided equally over the 36-month partnership.

The total funding pool for the opportunity is €2 million.

Organizations are not automatically guaranteed the amount they request. Following the assessment process, the adidas Foundation may offer a lower amount than the organization initially requested. Any adjustment will be discussed with the organization before the grant agreement is finalized.

The partnership is expected to begin in Q1 2027, with the grant start and first disbursement expected around March 2027.

What Is General Support Funding?

Unlike a grant that requires an organization to deliver one predefined project, The Next Move provides General Support funding.

This approach is designed to support the organization as a whole and give partners greater flexibility to determine their priorities.

Selected organizations can use the funding to support their charitable activities and organizational priorities, provided that the proposed expenditure remains within the eligible funding categories and complies with the Foundation’s requirements.

Organizations will identify a small number of priorities and planned activities and report on what the funding supported, what changed and how the money was used at category level.

This structure allows organizations to make adjustments during implementation when necessary, provided those adjustments remain within the approved scope and eligible uses of the grant.

What Can the Grant Be Used For?

The funding can support activities that directly advance an organization’s charitable work or help the organization deliver its work safely, effectively, inclusively and accountably.

Examples include:

Sport and Community Programs

Funding can support:

  • Community-based sport and physical activity programs
  • Inclusive sporting events
  • Participant activities
  • Community engagement
  • Outreach initiatives
  • Advocacy and awareness campaigns
  • Coalition-building and networking
  • Peer-learning activities
  • Participant transportation
  • Venue costs
  • Activity costs
  • Sports equipment
  • Adaptive equipment
  • Materials required for implementation

Organizations can also use eligible funding for staff time and related expenditure directly connected to charitable program activities.

Training and Capacity Building

Organizations may support training for:

  • Coaches
  • Facilitators
  • Community stakeholders
  • Staff members
  • Other individuals involved in program delivery

The objective is to strengthen the organization’s ability to deliver its programs effectively and safely.

Safeguarding and Participant Protection

Funding may also contribute to:

  • Safeguarding policies and procedures
  • Safeguarding training
  • Incident reporting systems
  • Referral procedures
  • Participant protection measures
  • Community protection measures
  • Inclusion and accessibility measures
  • Data protection
  • Information security

Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning

Organizations can also use eligible funding to strengthen their ability to understand and demonstrate their impact.

This includes:

  • Monitoring and evaluation
  • Accountability systems
  • Learning processes
  • Participant feedback
  • Community feedback
  • Outcome measurement
  • Evaluation activities
  • MEAL systems
  • Specialist advice related to charitable programs

Organizational and Administrative Costs

The grant includes an indirect cost recovery component equivalent to 20% of eligible direct costs.

This component is intended to recognize that strong programs require strong organizational systems behind them.

Eligible indirect costs can include areas such as:

  • General management and administration
  • Finance and accounting
  • Payroll and staff resources
  • General office expenses
  • Operating costs
  • Audit expenses
  • Insurance
  • Legal and compliance costs
  • Organization-wide IT systems
  • Administrative systems
  • General fundraising and income-generation activities

Organizations do not need to provide a separate expenditure breakdown for the indirect cost recovery component, although they must maintain appropriate financial records.

What Cannot Be Funded?

Although The Next Move provides flexible General Support funding, the grant is not completely unrestricted.

The following are not eligible:

  • Sub-granting or onward granting
  • Non-charitable activities
  • Activities outside the scope of the program
  • Commercial or primarily profit-seeking activities unrelated to charitable work
  • Support for political parties or candidates
  • Partisan campaigning
  • Lobbying outside the organization’s charitable mission and legally permissible activities
  • Religious proselytization or missionary work
  • Repayment of historic deficits
  • Unrelated loans
  • Penalties or liabilities unrelated to eligible charitable activities
  • Private benefits
  • Disproportionate remuneration
  • Illegal activities
  • Harmful or discriminatory activities
  • Sanctioned activities
  • Costs that cannot be properly documented

Organizations should therefore ensure that their intended use of funding is directly connected to their charitable mission and the objectives of The Next Move.

Who Can Apply?

The Next Move is not an individual scholarship or fellowship opportunity. It is specifically designed for non-profit organizations.

Eligible organizations must be legally registered and operating in one of the three eligible countries:

  • Brazil
  • Colombia
  • Argentina

Organizations must use sport or physical activity as a core vehicle for creating social impact.

This means sport should be central to the organization’s mission, programs and approach to creating positive change in the communities it serves.

Potentially eligible organizations include:

  • Community-based sport organizations
  • Sport-for-good organizations
  • Sport clubs with a demonstrated social impact mission
  • Sport foundations
  • Women’s sport networks
  • Advocacy organizations that combine advocacy with sport-based programs
  • Grassroots organizations delivering sport-based community services

Sport clubs can qualify where their charitable mission extends beyond simply providing sporting activities to their own members.

APPLY HERE

Organizational Eligibility Requirements

In addition to being a nonprofit organization operating in an eligible country, applicants must satisfy several organizational requirements.

The organization must:

  1. Be a legally registered non-governmental organization or equivalent established for charitable or public-benefit purposes under applicable national law.
  2. Have been registered and operational for at least two years in the country where it will implement its activities at the time of full application submission.
  3. Be legally permitted to receive foreign charitable funding under applicable local law.
  4. Not engage in partisan political activity or religious proselytization.
  5. Have a statutory purpose and core mission aligned with the objectives of The Next Move and the United by Sport program.
  6. Demonstrate commitment to non-discriminatory practices across race, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion and ethnicity.
  7. Have an annual grant request that does not exceed 50% of the organization’s total income in its most recent completed financial year.
  8. Have appropriate governance oversight and checks and balances, such as a board or equivalent oversight body.
  9. Have basic financial controls and reliable financial records.
  10. Be able to identify, track, document and report how the adidas Foundation’s funds are used.
  11. Have documented safeguarding policies and procedures.
  12. Have a safeguarding reporting mechanism explaining how concerns are raised and addressed.
  13. Have appropriate safer recruitment measures.
  14. Have documented rules covering expected and prohibited behavior, such as a Code of Conduct or Ethics Policy.
  15. Have guidance or established practices for protecting participant data and images.
  16. Not be subject to international sanctions or restrictions that would prevent a partnership.
  17. Be willing to undergo the Foundation’s due diligence process.
  18. Be willing to support communications and storytelling activities in accordance with the adidas Foundation’s ethical communication guidelines.
  19. Be committed to Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning processes.

Income Requirements Based on the Grant Requested

The organization must also have an annual income proportionate to the amount of funding it is requesting.

Based on the most recent financial statement, covering 2025 or 2024, the requirements are:

Organizations requesting €150,000

  • Minimum annual income: €100,000
  • Maximum annual income: €1.5 million

Organizations requesting €200,000

  • Minimum annual income: €135,000
  • Maximum annual income: €2 million

Organizations requesting €250,000

  • Minimum annual income: €165,000
  • Maximum annual income: €2.5 million

These financial requirements are intended to ensure that the level of funding is proportionate to the organization’s existing financial capacity.

Geographic Eligibility

The Next Move is specifically open to organizations operating in:

Brazil, Colombia and Argentina.

Organizations must be legally registered and implementing their activities in the country where they are applying.

Importantly, applicants cannot submit one application covering multiple countries. Each application should focus on one country of implementation.

Organizations based outside Brazil, Colombia or Argentina should not assume they are eligible simply because they work internationally. The guidelines specifically identify these three countries as the geographic scope of the call.

Race and Diversity Eligibility

The opportunity does not specify a particular race or ethnic group that applicants must belong to because the applicants are organizations rather than individuals.

However, eligible organizations must demonstrate a commitment to non-discriminatory practices across:

  • Race
  • Gender
  • Gender identity
  • Sexual orientation
  • Age
  • Disability
  • Religion
  • Ethnicity

The program itself is designed around inclusion, equality, safety and social cohesion.

The Application Process

The Next Move uses a two-stage application process designed to allow organizations to determine whether the opportunity is suitable before investing significant time in a full application.

Stage 1: Expression of Interest

Organizations begin by submitting an Expression of Interest (EOI) through an online application form.

The EOI includes:

  • Eligibility screening
  • Questions about the organization
  • Questions about the organization’s work
  • Required document uploads

The eligibility screening includes yes/no questions covering the non-negotiable organizational requirements.

Stage 2: Full Application

Only organizations that are shortlisted following the EOI stage will move to the full application stage.

Shortlisted organizations may be asked to:

  • Complete a self-assessment
  • Develop a proposed plan for the first year
  • Provide an indicative first-year budget
  • Answer additional questions
  • Participate in an interview with the adidas Foundation

The Foundation may also arrange a short call to clarify outstanding information.

This approach means applicants do not have to prepare a lengthy full proposal at the initial stage.

How Applications Are Assessed

After organizations submit their Expressions of Interest, the adidas Foundation reviews applications against the eligibility criteria.

The process includes:

  1. EOI submission
  2. Eligibility screening
  3. Conflict-of-interest checks
  4. Shortlisting
  5. Full application
  6. Interview and additional submissions
  7. Review and final selection
  8. Due diligence
  9. Contracting
  10. Grant disbursement

The Foundation intends to select a minimum of eight organizations to receive grants, subject to successful completion of the subsequent due diligence process.

Due Diligence Requirements

Being selected following the assessment process does not immediately guarantee funding.

Organizations selected for funding must successfully complete the adidas Foundation’s organizational due diligence process before funding is formally confirmed.

The due diligence process examines areas including:

Legal Status and Governance

Organizations may need to provide:

  • Registration or incorporation documents
  • Current proof of legal existence
  • Tax-status documentation
  • Governing documents
  • Organizational charts
  • Governance arrangements
  • Information about authorized representatives

Financial Management

The Foundation may assess:

  • Financial position
  • Financial sustainability
  • Sources of income
  • Financial statements
  • Audit reports
  • Accounting systems
  • Financial controls
  • Approval procedures
  • Grant-tracking systems
  • Financial records

Safeguarding

Organizations may need to demonstrate:

  • Safeguarding policies
  • Reporting mechanisms
  • Incident-management procedures
  • Safer recruitment practices
  • Safeguarding responsibilities
  • Training arrangements

Integrity and Organizational Standards

The review can also include:

  • Codes of conduct
  • Ethics policies
  • Whistleblowing systems
  • Complaints mechanisms
  • Anti-fraud measures
  • Anti-bribery measures
  • Data protection procedures
  • Public-domain reviews
  • Sanctions screening
  • Adverse-media screening
  • Other integrity checks

Organizations that do not meet the Foundation’s due diligence requirements will not be eligible for funding.

Community of Practice and Peer Learning

Selected organizations will participate in a Community of Practice designed to encourage peer learning, exchange and collective reflection.

The Community of Practice can help participating organizations:

  • Share experiences
  • Exchange promising practices
  • Strengthen organizational capacity
  • Learn from other organizations
  • Reflect on implementation challenges
  • Develop approaches related to gender equity
  • Share lessons around gender-based violence prevention
  • Explore safe sport practices
  • Strengthen inclusion
  • Improve community-building through sport

Organizations are encouraged to designate at least one relevant staff member to participate.

This could include staff working in:

  • Programs
  • Safeguarding
  • MEAL
  • Organizational development
  • Leadership
  • Other relevant areas

Organizations are encouraged to plan for up to 60 hours per year, or approximately five hours per month, for Community of Practice activities, peer exchanges, learning events and related preparation.

Participation costs, including relevant staff time, can be covered through the grant and should be reflected in the organization’s proposed use of funds.

Communications and Storytelling

Selected organizations should also be prepared to participate in communications and storytelling activities connected to the partnership.

This may involve:

  • Contributing to storytelling pieces
  • Providing relevant content
  • Following approval processes
  • Following the adidas Foundation’s ethical communication guidelines
  • Respecting brand guidelines
  • Providing feedback and approvals within five business days

The Foundation will provide selected organizations with the relevant communication and brand guidance.

Reporting and Evaluation

The reporting requirements are designed to be proportionate and focused on learning rather than requiring organizations to report every individual expenditure line.

During the three-year partnership, selected organizations can expect several reporting and learning requirements.

At the Start

Organizations will complete an Organizational Self-Assessment to identify areas for growth.

During the Partnership

There will be:

  • Bi-annual check-in calls with the Foundation
  • Annual narrative reporting
  • Annual financial reporting at category level
  • Annual reach data
  • Photos and videos from activities, where appropriate and with consent
  • Annual partner feedback

Financial reporting will show planned and actual expenditure, significant variances and a transaction tracker.

Individual receipts and invoices do not have to be submitted as part of routine annual reporting, but organizations must retain the relevant documentation because the Foundation may request supporting records.

At the End

Organizations will complete:

  • An organizational self-assessment
  • Change stories at organizational and individual level

They may also be invited to participate in a learning exercise during or after the funding period.

Grant Disbursement

The three-year grant period begins after the grant agreement is signed.

The grant is expected to begin in Q1 2027, with the first disbursement expected around March 2027.

Funding will be distributed in three instalments over the three-year partnership.

The first instalment will be released after:

  • Successful completion of due diligence
  • Approval of the initial plan
  • Approval of the budget
  • Signing of the grant agreement

Subsequent instalments will normally depend on the Foundation reviewing and accepting reporting from the previous period and approving the updated plan and budget.

Key Dates and Deadline

Applicants should pay close attention to the following dates:

  • Call launch: 7 September 2026
  • Q&A Webinar: 21 September 2026 at 11:00 AM BRT
  • EOI submission deadline: 4 October 2026 at 11:59 PM BRT
  • Screening and shortlisting: October 2026
  • EOI outcome notification: October 2026
  • Full application, interviews and submissions: November 2026
  • Review and final selection: December 2026
  • Vetting and due diligence: December 2026/January 2027
  • Contracting: January/February 2027
  • Expected grant start and first disbursement: March 2027

The deadline to submit the Expression of Interest is 4 October 2026 at 11:59 PM BRT. Dates after the EOI deadline are indicative and may be adjusted by the adidas Foundation.

Visit HERE to learn more about  The Next Move Grant 2026

How to Apply

Eligible organizations should begin with the Expression of Interest (EOI) stage.

The application process requires organizations to provide information about their legal status, organizational structure, work, eligibility and activities, together with the required supporting documents.

The guidelines state that English is the working language throughout the application process, including the application, supporting documents, interview and partnership.

At the EOI stage, unofficial translations of documents are sufficient.

Organizations should ensure that the information submitted accurately reflects their own experience, activities and organizational context. Applicants are encouraged to provide specific and concrete examples from their work.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Organizations considering The Next Move should assess themselves against the eligibility requirements before submitting an EOI.

In particular, applicants should confirm that they:

  • Are a legally registered nonprofit organization.
  • Have operated for at least two years in the implementation country.
  • Are legally permitted to receive foreign charitable funding.
  • Operate in Brazil, Colombia or Argentina.
  • Use sport or physical activity as a central part of their social-impact approach.
  • Work directly with communities.
  • Do not intend to sub-grant the funding.
  • Have appropriate governance structures.
  • Have adequate financial controls.
  • Meet the applicable annual-income requirement.
  • Have safeguarding systems in place.
  • Have appropriate data protection practices.
  • Can participate in monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning.
  • Are prepared to undergo organizational due diligence.
  • Can commit to a three-year partnership.

Organizations should also ensure that their requested grant amount is proportionate to their annual income and that their planned activities clearly align with the objectives of The Next Move.

Who Qualifies for This Opportunity?

Qualifying category: Nonprofit organizations, NGOs, sport organizations, sport clubs, foundations, women’s sport networks and advocacy organizations that use sport or physical activity as a core vehicle for social impact.

Required organizational qualifications

Applicants must generally:

  • Be legally registered as a nonprofit/non-governmental or equivalent charitable/public-benefit organization.
  • Have operated for at least two years in the country of implementation.
  • Be legally allowed to receive foreign charitable funding.
  • Directly implement activities in the country of operation.
  • Use sport or physical activity as a central part of their mission and programs.
  • Align their mission with The Next Move and United by Sport objectives.
  • Meet the applicable annual-income requirements.
  • Have appropriate governance and financial systems.
  • Have safeguarding and reporting mechanisms.
  • Demonstrate commitment to nondiscrimination.
  • Be willing to undergo due diligence and integrity screening.
  • Commit to the three-year partnership and MEAL requirements.

Eligible countries/regions

The opportunity is open specifically to organizations implementing activities in:

Brazil, Colombia and Argentina.

Applications must focus on one country of implementation rather than combining multiple countries in one application.

Race and ethnicity

There is no specific racial or ethnic group requirement for applicants. The applicant is an organization rather than an individual. However, eligible organizations must demonstrate nondiscriminatory practices across race, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion and ethnicity.

Conclusion

The Next Move Grant 2026 provides a significant opportunity for established nonprofit organizations in Brazil, Colombia and Argentina that are using sport to tackle social challenges and build stronger communities.

With grants of €150,000, €200,000 or €250,000 distributed over three years, the program can support much more than individual sporting activities. Eligible funding can contribute to community programs, equipment, participant activities, training, safeguarding, monitoring and evaluation, organizational capacity and appropriate administrative costs.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to organizations addressing gender-based violence, discrimination, exclusion, unequal participation and harmful gender norms through sport.

Organizations interested in applying should carefully review their eligibility, financial capacity, governance, safeguarding systems and alignment with the program before submitting an Expression of Interest.

The key deadline is 4 October 2026 at 11:59 PM BRT. Since the application process begins with an Expression of Interest and shortlisted organizations subsequently move to a more detailed application and due diligence process, eligible organizations should begin preparing their documentation well before the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Neukom Institute at Dartmouth College has announced the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Competition 2027, an exceptional opportunity for recent PhD graduates and emerging scholars whose research crosses traditional academic boundaries and incorporates computation as a significant intellectual, methodological, or practical component.

The prestigious fellowship is designed for highly motivated interdisciplinary researchers who are interested in exploring complex questions that cannot easily be confined to a single academic discipline. Successful candidates will receive the opportunity to conduct independent research at Dartmouth College while working across departments, collaborating with faculty mentors, teaching seminars, and becoming part of a vibrant intellectual community focused on computational thinking and interdisciplinary scholarship.

The Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship positions are scheduled to begin on September 1, 2027. Selected Fellows will receive appointments lasting two years, with the possibility of requesting a third year. For the 2027–2028 academic year, Neukom Fellows will receive a stipend of $70,000, alongside additional financial support for equipment, travel, and research materials.

The competition provides an important platform for scholars whose work sits at the intersection of disciplines and computation. Whether computation serves as a methodological tool, a conceptual framework, or an explicit component of a research project, the fellowship encourages innovative approaches that challenge conventional academic boundaries.

About the Dartmouth Neukom Institute Postdoctoral Fellows Program

The Neukom Institute at Dartmouth College supports research and intellectual exploration at the intersection of computation and multiple academic disciplines. Its Postdoctoral Fellows Program brings together scholars whose work demonstrates the potential to bridge fields, develop new approaches to research, and expand how computational ideas can contribute to the understanding of complex problems.

The fellowship is particularly suited to researchers who do not fit neatly into traditional academic categories. Applicants may come from disciplines across the sciences, humanities, social sciences, arts, engineering, and other fields, provided they can demonstrate a meaningful connection between their research interests and the broader theme of computation.

A central feature of the Neukom Fellowship is its interdisciplinary structure. Fellows are expected to engage with faculty members and academic departments across Dartmouth College rather than working exclusively within a single disciplinary environment.

The program seeks individuals who can demonstrate both:

  • A history of successful collaboration across disciplinary boundaries; and
  • Strong evidence of independence, initiative, and the ability to develop original research ideas.

This balance between collaboration and independent scholarship makes the fellowship particularly attractive to researchers seeking to establish themselves as leaders in emerging interdisciplinary fields.

Why the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship Is Unique

Many postdoctoral opportunities are structured around a specific department, laboratory, or narrowly defined research area. The Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship takes a broader approach by encouraging scholars to connect different academic perspectives through computational research and thinking.

Successful Fellows will have the opportunity to:

  • Conduct independent interdisciplinary research.
  • Work with faculty members from two Dartmouth College departments.
  • Develop relationships across multiple academic disciplines.
  • Explore innovative research questions.
  • Engage with computational concepts and methodologies.
  • Teach one seminar course each year.
  • Access financial support for research activities.
  • Participate in Dartmouth’s academic and intellectual community.
  • Build professional networks with scholars across different disciplines.
  • Develop new approaches that move beyond conventional academic paradigms.

The program recognizes that some of the most important contemporary research challenges require perspectives from multiple disciplines. By supporting scholars who can work across these boundaries, the Neukom Institute aims to encourage new forms of intellectual collaboration and discovery.

Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship Funding and Financial Benefits

One of the major advantages of the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship is the financial support provided to selected candidates.

For the 2027–2028 academic year, Neukom Fellows will receive a stipend of:

$70,000

In addition to the annual stipend, Fellows can access additional funding for important research-related needs.

Additional support may be available for:

  • Research equipment.
  • Academic travel.
  • Conference participation.
  • Research materials.
  • Other resources necessary to support the Fellow’s scholarly work.

This financial structure allows Fellows to focus significantly on their research and professional development while receiving institutional support for activities that contribute to their academic projects.

The fellowship appointment is initially structured as a two-year position, providing researchers with substantial time to develop and advance an interdisciplinary research agenda. Fellows may also have the option to request a third year, depending on program arrangements and individual circumstances.

Fellowship Structure and Academic Experience

The Neukom Fellows Program provides more than financial support. It offers a comprehensive academic environment designed to help emerging scholars expand their research networks and intellectual perspectives.

1. Two-Year Fellowship Appointment

Selected candidates will receive appointments lasting two years. This extended period gives Fellows the opportunity to undertake substantial research projects rather than focusing only on short-term academic activities.

The possibility of requesting a third year may provide additional flexibility for scholars whose research requires further development.

2. Mentorship Across Two Departments

One of the defining features of the program is interdisciplinary mentorship.

Neukom Fellows will be mentored by faculty members representing two different departments at Dartmouth College. This structure encourages Fellows to actively engage with different intellectual traditions and methodologies.

Working across departments can help researchers:

  • Develop broader perspectives.
  • Establish collaborations outside their original discipline.
  • Access different methodological approaches.
  • Test research ideas with diverse academic audiences.
  • Build interdisciplinary professional networks.
  • Develop innovative approaches to complex research questions.

3. Departmental Residence

While Fellows will work across two academic departments, they will take up residence in one department at Dartmouth College.

This arrangement provides Fellows with an academic home while simultaneously allowing them to maintain meaningful engagement with another disciplinary environment.

4. Teaching Opportunity

Neukom Fellows will teach one seminar course each year on a subject related to their interests and expertise.

This teaching component provides an opportunity for Fellows to:

  • Develop university-level teaching experience.
  • Design an original seminar.
  • Share their research interests with students.
  • Explore interdisciplinary topics in a classroom setting.
  • Strengthen their academic portfolio.
  • Gain valuable experience for future faculty and research positions.

5. Focus on Research

Apart from the teaching seminar, Fellows do not have additional duties specified by the program.

This allows successful candidates to devote substantial attention to their research projects, collaborations, and scholarly development.

Research Focus: Computation and Interdisciplinary Scholarship

A central requirement of the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship is a meaningful connection between an applicant’s research and the theme of computation.

Importantly, computation does not necessarily have to be interpreted narrowly.

According to the program description, computation may serve as:

  • A framing concept for intellectual exploration.
  • An explicit methodological component of research.
  • A tool for investigating complex questions.
  • A foundation for interdisciplinary collaboration.
  • A means of connecting different academic fields.

This broad approach makes the fellowship relevant to researchers working in a wide range of disciplines.

For example, applicants may explore intersections between computation and areas such as:

  • Computer science.
  • Artificial intelligence.
  • Data science.
  • Digital humanities.
  • Computational social science.
  • Mathematics.
  • Engineering.
  • Biology.
  • Environmental studies.
  • Economics.
  • Philosophy.
  • Linguistics.
  • Media studies.
  • Creative arts.
  • Public policy.
  • History.
  • Literature.
  • Psychology.
  • Physics.
  • Education.
  • Communication studies.
  • Cultural studies.

The specific research area does not need to belong exclusively to a computational discipline. However, applicants must clearly demonstrate how computation meaningfully intersects with their proposed work.

Eligibility Requirements for the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027

The Neukom Institute welcomes applications from scholars across different academic backgrounds.

To be eligible for the fellowship, applicants should meet the following requirements.

Academic Qualification

Applicants must hold or expect to receive one of the following qualifications by September 2027:

  • PhD in any discipline.
  • Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA).
  • Master of Fine Arts (MFA), where applicable to the fellowship requirements.

The program specifically indicates that candidates may be expected to complete their doctoral qualification by September 2027.

This makes the fellowship particularly relevant for:

  • Recent PhD graduates.
  • Final-stage doctoral candidates.
  • Emerging scholars preparing to transition into postdoctoral research.
  • Researchers seeking an interdisciplinary academic environment after completing their doctoral studies.

Research Connection to Computation

Applicants must demonstrate research interests that strongly intersect with the broader theme of computation.

Candidates should clearly explain:

  • How computation relates to their research.
  • How computational ideas, methods, or frameworks contribute to their work.
  • Why interdisciplinary collaboration is important for their proposed research.
  • How the fellowship environment would strengthen their intellectual development.

Interest in Multidisciplinary Research

The Neukom Institute is specifically looking for scholars who are interested in working beyond traditional disciplinary boundaries.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate:

  • Experience collaborating across disciplines.
  • Interest in multidisciplinary research.
  • Openness to different academic perspectives.
  • Ability to communicate with researchers from different fields.
  • Willingness to explore new methodologies and intellectual frameworks.

Independent Thinking and Initiative

Although collaboration is important, successful applicants must also demonstrate independence.

The program seeks candidates with evidence of:

  • Original thinking.
  • Research initiative.
  • Intellectual independence.
  • Leadership potential.
  • The ability to develop and pursue innovative research questions.

Ability to Think Beyond Traditional Paradigms

The fellowship strongly emphasizes innovative and unconventional thinking.

Applicants should demonstrate the capacity to:

  • Challenge traditional academic boundaries.
  • Connect ideas from different disciplines.
  • Develop creative research methodologies.
  • Explore emerging questions.
  • Think critically about established assumptions.
  • Build new intellectual frameworks.

Required Application Materials

Applicants for the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Program must prepare several important documents.

Candidates are encouraged to begin preparing their applications early, particularly because identifying and contacting potential Dartmouth faculty mentors may require significant research and communication.

The required application materials include the following.

1. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a comprehensive academic curriculum vitae.

The CV should clearly highlight relevant experience, including:

  • Academic qualifications.
  • Research experience.
  • Publications.
  • Academic appointments.
  • Teaching experience.
  • Research collaborations.
  • Conferences and presentations.
  • Awards and honors.
  • Technical or methodological skills.
  • Interdisciplinary projects.

Candidates should ensure that their CV clearly demonstrates their academic development and capacity to contribute to an interdisciplinary research environment.

2. Publications List

Applicants are required to provide a list of publications.

This may include:

  • Journal articles.
  • Book chapters.
  • Books.
  • Conference papers.
  • Working papers.
  • Research reports.
  • Other relevant scholarly publications.

Where appropriate, candidates should clearly identify publications that demonstrate interdisciplinary or computational aspects of their work.

3. Statement of Research Interests

Applicants must submit a statement of research interests with a maximum length of two pages.

The statement should include a short description of the research the applicant would like to pursue as a Neukom Fellow.

A strong research statement should clearly address:

  • The central research question.
  • The importance of the proposed research.
  • The relationship between the project and computation.
  • The interdisciplinary nature of the work.
  • The proposed methodology.
  • Expected research outcomes.
  • Potential academic or societal contributions.
  • Why Dartmouth College provides an appropriate environment for the research.

Because the fellowship is highly interdisciplinary, applicants should ensure that their research statement is understandable to readers from multiple academic backgrounds.

4. Proposed Departments and Faculty Mentors

Applicants must describe:

  • Which Dartmouth College departments they are interested in working with.
  • Which Dartmouth faculty members they would like to collaborate with.
  • Why these academic connections are relevant to their proposed research.
  • How working across multiple departments would enhance their scholarship.

The Neukom Institute strongly encourages applicants to research Dartmouth’s departments and faculty listings when preparing this section.

Candidates are also strongly encouraged to identify potential faculty mentors and contact them while developing their applications.

This is an important part of the application strategy because demonstrating a clear understanding of Dartmouth’s academic environment can strengthen the connection between the applicant’s proposed research and the fellowship.

Applicants should therefore consider:

  1. Identifying departments relevant to their research.
  2. Reviewing faculty profiles.
  3. Reading about faculty research interests.
  4. Identifying potential interdisciplinary connections.
  5. Contacting prospective mentors where appropriate.
  6. Explaining clearly how those academic relationships could support the proposed research.

5. Three Referees and Letters of Recommendation

Applicants must provide details for three referees.

The letters of recommendation should speak directly to the aims and objectives of the fellowship.

Applicants will provide the referees’ email addresses through the application system. Referees will then receive an email with access to upload their letters directly.

Applicants will not have access to the submitted recommendation letters.

Candidates should carefully select referees who can discuss areas such as:

  • Research ability.
  • Academic independence.
  • Interdisciplinary experience.
  • Collaborative skills.
  • Intellectual creativity.
  • Leadership potential.
  • Ability to develop innovative research.
  • Suitability for a postdoctoral academic environment.

Although applicants are encouraged to have their applications completed by the main deadline, referees have an additional period to submit their letters.

6. Optional Writing Sample or Creative Work

Applicants may optionally submit one paper written in English.

The work may be:

  • Published; or
  • Unpublished.

Applicants whose work involves creative practice may submit comparable creative work instead.

A strong optional submission could provide additional evidence of:

  • Research quality.
  • Writing ability.
  • Originality.
  • Methodological expertise.
  • Interdisciplinary thinking.

7. Optional Teaching Statement

Applicants may also submit a teaching statement.

This can be particularly useful for candidates who want to demonstrate their readiness to teach the required annual seminar.

A teaching statement may discuss:

  • Teaching philosophy.
  • Previous teaching experience.
  • Approaches to interdisciplinary education.
  • Student engagement strategies.
  • Proposed seminar ideas.

8. Optional Cover Letter

Candidates may submit an optional cover letter.

A well-written cover letter could briefly summarize:

  • Academic background.
  • Research interests.
  • Interdisciplinary experience.
  • Connection to computation.
  • Motivation for applying.
  • Why the Neukom Fellowship is an appropriate next step.

Importance of Contacting Potential Dartmouth Mentors

One of the strongest recommendations provided by the program is that applicants should actively identify and contact prospective mentors at Dartmouth College.

Candidates are encouraged to begin making these academic connections while drafting their applications.

This approach can be valuable because it allows applicants to:

  • Better understand Dartmouth’s research environment.
  • Identify faculty whose expertise aligns with their work.
  • Develop stronger interdisciplinary research proposals.
  • Explain why specific departments are relevant.
  • Demonstrate genuine interest in collaboration.
  • Clarify how their proposed research could fit within Dartmouth’s academic community.

Applicants should approach potential mentors professionally and thoughtfully.

Before contacting a faculty member, candidates should:

  1. Carefully review the faculty member’s research profile.
  2. Understand their major research interests.
  3. Identify a genuine connection with their own work.
  4. Prepare a concise introduction.
  5. Briefly explain the proposed research idea.
  6. Explain why the faculty member’s expertise is relevant.
  7. Avoid sending generic messages to multiple academics.

Early preparation is particularly important because identifying appropriate mentors and developing meaningful academic connections may take time.

Residence Requirement

Neukom Fellows are generally expected to be in residence at Dartmouth College.

The primary exception relates to travel associated with:

  • Research activities.
  • Academic conferences.
  • Other approved scholarly engagements.

Candidates should therefore be prepared to participate actively in Dartmouth’s academic community during the fellowship period.

Being in residence provides Fellows with opportunities to:

  • Meet regularly with faculty mentors.
  • Participate in academic discussions.
  • Collaborate with researchers.
  • Engage with students.
  • Attend seminars and events.
  • Build interdisciplinary networks.

Important Dates and Application Timeline

Applicants should pay close attention to the official competition schedule.

Application Site Opens

August 1, 2026

The online application system becomes available through Interfolio.

Application Deadline

December 1, 2026

Applicants should submit their complete applications by this date.

The program indicates that application review will begin on December 1, 2026.

Letters of Recommendation Deadline

December 8, 2026

Letters of recommendation must be submitted no later than this date.

Applicants should contact their referees well in advance to ensure they have sufficient time to prepare strong recommendation letters.

Fellowship Start Date

September 1, 2027

Successful Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows are expected to begin their appointments.

How to Apply for the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027

The application process is completed online through the Interfolio application platform.

Interested candidates should follow these general steps.

Step 1: Review the Fellowship Requirements

Carefully read all eligibility criteria and application requirements before beginning the application.

Ensure that your academic qualifications and research interests align with the program.

Step 2: Develop Your Research Proposal

Prepare a strong research statement explaining:

  • Your proposed research.
  • Its interdisciplinary nature.
  • Its connection to computation.
  • Why the research is important.
  • How Dartmouth College would support the project.

Step 3: Identify Relevant Dartmouth Departments

Explore Dartmouth College’s academic departments and identify those connected to your research interests.

Consider how different departments could contribute complementary perspectives to your project.

Step 4: Identify Potential Faculty Mentors

Review Dartmouth faculty profiles and identify scholars whose research aligns with your proposed work.

The program strongly encourages applicants to explore potential academic connections while preparing their applications.

Step 5: Contact Potential Mentors

Where appropriate, reach out professionally to prospective mentors.

Explain your research interests and your interest in the interdisciplinary environment provided by the Neukom Fellowship.

Step 6: Prepare Your Supporting Documents

Compile the required materials, including:

  • Curriculum vitae.
  • Publications list.
  • Two-page research statement.
  • Description of relevant departments and faculty mentors.
  • Referee information.

Consider including optional materials where they strengthen your application.

Step 7: Notify Your Referees Early

Contact your three referees well before the deadline.

Provide them with:

  • Information about the fellowship.
  • Your research proposal.
  • Your CV.
  • Relevant application deadlines.

This will help them prepare letters that are specifically tailored to the aims of the Neukom Fellowship.

Step 8: Submit Your Application Online

Applications can be submitted through Interfolio once the application system opens.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day, as early submission provides time to address any technical issues.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

The Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship is designed for ambitious scholars working at the intersection of disciplines. Applicants should therefore ensure that their applications clearly communicate both academic depth and interdisciplinary vision.

Clearly Explain the Computational Connection

Do not assume that reviewers will automatically understand how your research relates to computation.

Clearly explain whether computation functions as:

  • A research methodology.
  • A theoretical framework.
  • A conceptual lens.
  • A practical tool.
  • A core component of your proposed project.

Demonstrate Genuine Interdisciplinarity

Simply mentioning multiple disciplines may not be sufficient.

Applicants should demonstrate how different fields will actively contribute to the proposed research.

Explain:

  • What each discipline contributes.
  • Why one discipline alone is insufficient.
  • How interdisciplinary collaboration will create new insights.

Balance Collaboration and Independence

The fellowship seeks candidates who can collaborate effectively while also pursuing independent scholarship.

Use examples from your academic experience to demonstrate both qualities.

Research Dartmouth Thoroughly

A strong application should demonstrate why Dartmouth College is particularly suitable for the proposed project.

Avoid generic statements.

Instead, identify:

  • Relevant departments.
  • Potential faculty collaborators.
  • Academic resources.
  • Interdisciplinary opportunities.

Select Referees Strategically

Choose referees who understand your research trajectory and can provide detailed examples of your abilities.

Ideally, recommendation letters should reinforce the themes emphasized throughout the application.

Begin Preparation Early

Because the application involves:

  • Developing a research proposal.
  • Identifying multiple departments.
  • Researching Dartmouth faculty.
  • Contacting potential mentors.
  • Coordinating recommendation letters.

Applicants should begin preparing well before the December deadline.

Diversity and Equal Opportunity

Dartmouth College states that it is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer with a strong commitment to diversity.

The institution encourages applications from a broad spectrum of individuals, including:

  • Women.
  • Persons of color.
  • Persons with disabilities.
  • Veterans.
  • Other legally protected groups.

This commitment reflects the Neukom Institute’s interest in building a diverse intellectual community that brings together different perspectives, experiences, academic backgrounds, and approaches to research.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship may be particularly suitable for scholars who answer yes to several of the following questions:

  • Are you completing a PhD or recently completed doctoral research?
  • Does your work intersect meaningfully with computation?
  • Does your research cross traditional academic boundaries?
  • Are you interested in working with scholars from multiple disciplines?
  • Do you have an innovative research idea that requires diverse academic perspectives?
  • Are you comfortable developing independent research projects?
  • Do you want postdoctoral teaching experience?
  • Are you interested in becoming part of an interdisciplinary academic community?
  • Can you identify Dartmouth faculty members whose expertise could strengthen your research?

If these characteristics align with your academic goals, the Neukom Fellowship could provide an important opportunity to develop an innovative research agenda.

Key Benefits of the Dartmouth Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship

Successful Fellows can benefit from a combination of financial support, research opportunities, mentorship, teaching experience, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Key benefits include:

  • A $70,000 stipend for 2027–2028.
  • A two-year fellowship appointment.
  • The possibility of requesting a third year.
  • Additional support for equipment.
  • Funding support for research travel.
  • Support for research materials.
  • Mentorship from faculty in two Dartmouth departments.
  • An opportunity to conduct interdisciplinary research.
  • Residence within Dartmouth College’s academic community.
  • The opportunity to teach one seminar course per year.
  • No additional duties beyond the specified fellowship responsibilities.
  • Opportunities to collaborate across traditional academic boundaries.
  • Access to an intellectually diverse research environment.
  • Professional development through research and teaching.
  • Opportunities to expand academic networks.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Competition 2027 is: December 1, 2026

Applicants should note that letters of recommendation are due no later than: December 8, 2026

The application portal opens on August 1, 2026, and selected Fellows are expected to begin their appointments on September 1, 2027.

APPLY HERE

How to Access the Official Application

Interested applicants should submit their applications online through the Interfolio application platform after the application portal opens.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Dartmouth Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Program 2027.

Conclusion

The Dartmouth Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Program 2027 represents an outstanding opportunity for emerging scholars whose work challenges traditional disciplinary boundaries and engages meaningfully with the broad field of computation. With a $70,000 stipend, additional research support, mentorship across two academic departments, teaching opportunities, and a two-year appointment with the potential for extension, the fellowship provides an exceptional environment for developing ambitious interdisciplinary research.

The program is particularly attractive because it welcomes researchers from diverse academic disciplines rather than restricting participation to a single field. Candidates who can demonstrate a strong connection between their research and computation, an interest in multidisciplinary collaboration, and the ability to think independently and creatively are encouraged to consider applying.

Prospective applicants should begin preparing early by refining their research ideas, identifying relevant Dartmouth departments, connecting with potential faculty mentors, and securing strong recommendation letters. Given the fellowship’s emphasis on innovative scholarship and interdisciplinary collaboration, a carefully developed application that clearly communicates both intellectual originality and the value of cross-disciplinary research could significantly strengthen a candidate’s prospects.

With applications closing on December 1, 2026, eligible researchers have an opportunity to position themselves for a transformative postdoctoral experience at one of the leading institutions supporting interdisciplinary research at the intersection of computation and the wider academic world.
