item.content:encoded:
The Global Water and Climate Adaptation Centre – Aachen, Bangkok, Chennai, Dresden (ABCD-Centre) has opened applications for the ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarships 2027, an opportunity designed to support doctoral researchers from developing countries whose work addresses pressing challenges related to water security, climate change adaptation, ecosystem resilience, sustainable development, and environmental management.

The 2027 scholarship call will support two doctoral students through a nine-month research stay in Germany. Successful applicants will have the opportunity to conduct research at one of three participating host institutions: RWTH Aachen University in Aachen, Technische Universität Dresden, or UNU Resource Nexus in Dresden.

The research stays are scheduled to take place from March 1, 2027, to November 30, 2027.

The programme is particularly valuable for PhD researchers who want to strengthen their academic and research experience in an international environment while developing research that can ultimately be translated into practical solutions, policy recommendations, and real-world approaches to water and climate adaptation challenges.

About the Global Water and Climate Adaptation Centre

The Global Water and Climate Adaptation Centre – Aachen, Bangkok, Chennai, Dresden (ABCD-Centre) is an international collaborative initiative bringing together leading academic and research institutions in Europe and Asia.

The consortium includes:

  • RWTH Aachen University
  • Asian Institute of Technology
  • Indian Institute of Technology Madras
  • United Nations University – Institute for Integrated Management of Material Fluxes and Resources (UNU Resource Nexus)
  • Technische Universität Dresden

The Centre seeks to address some of the world’s most urgent and interconnected environmental challenges, particularly those involving water security and climate adaptation.

Its work combines research, education, international collaboration, and knowledge transfer, with a strong emphasis on ensuring that scientific findings can move beyond academic publications and contribute to practical solutions.

A major objective of the ABCD-Centre is to develop the next generation of Future Environmental Leaders. These researchers are expected not only to produce high-quality scientific work but also to help translate research findings into applications that can benefit communities, institutions, policymakers, and other stakeholders.

About the ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarships 2027

For the 2027 cycle, the ABCD-Centre is offering two scholarships, each supporting a nine-month research stay in Germany.

The scholarships are intended for doctoral students from developing countries who are already undertaking PhD studies at universities in developing countries.

The programme provides selected researchers with an opportunity to temporarily conduct part of their doctoral research at an internationally recognised German research institution.

Applicants are required to indicate their preferred host university when applying.

The available host institutions are:

  1. RWTH Aachen University – Aachen, Germany
  2. Technische Universität Dresden – Dresden, Germany
  3. UNU Resource Nexus – United Nations University Institute for Integrated Management of Material Fluxes and Resources, Dresden, Germany

The research stay is planned for:

March 1, 2027 – November 30, 2027

Applicants who are able and willing to spend the full nine-month period in Germany are given preference during the selection process.

Research Areas and Thematic Clusters

Applicants are encouraged to develop research proposals that fit within the three interconnected research clusters of the ABCD-Centre.

Cluster I: Water Security and Water Resources Management

The first cluster focuses on challenges surrounding water security and the sustainable management and provision of water resources.

Research areas include:

  • Water security
  • Water resources management
  • Secure water supply
  • Water treatment
  • Innovative approaches to water management
  • Technologies and approaches for improving access to and sustainability of water resources

This cluster may be particularly relevant to researchers investigating how societies can improve water availability, water quality, infrastructure, and resource management in the context of growing environmental pressures.

Cluster II: Ecosystem Resilience and Nature-Based Adaptation

The second cluster focuses on strengthening ecosystems and exploring nature-based approaches to climate adaptation.

Potential areas include:

  • Ecosystem resilience
  • Nature-based solutions
  • Climate adaptation
  • Environmental restoration
  • Sustainable ecosystem management
  • Innovative monitoring systems
  • Adaptation measures that work with natural processes

Researchers working on environmental systems and solutions that use or strengthen natural ecosystems to address climate risks are encouraged to consider this research cluster.

Cluster III: Transfer Strategies for Climate Adaptation

The third cluster focuses on how climate adaptation research can be transferred into society and translated into practical action.

It includes areas such as:

  • Traditional knowledge
  • Local economies
  • Societal acceptance
  • Climate adaptation strategies
  • Knowledge transfer
  • Policy development
  • Community-based approaches
  • Translating scientific findings into practical solutions

This cluster recognises that effective climate adaptation requires more than scientific innovation. Solutions must also be socially acceptable, economically realistic, culturally appropriate, and capable of being implemented by communities and institutions.

Priority Research Topics for the 2027 Scholarship

Although the scholarship is open to a broad range of research topics connected to the ABCD-Centre’s thematic clusters, priority will be given to proposals addressing five specific areas.

Topic A: Modelling Water Infrastructure, Digitalization and Habitat Modelling

This area includes research into:

  • Water infrastructure modelling
  • Innovative digitalisation methods
  • Digital twins
  • Habitat modelling

Applicants working on the use of digital technologies, modelling systems, simulations, or related tools to improve water infrastructure or environmental management may find this theme particularly relevant.

Topic B: Innovative Monitoring for Ecosystem Resilience and Nature-Based Adaptation

This topic focuses on improved methods for monitoring ecosystems and understanding their resilience to environmental change.

Research could address:

  • Innovative environmental monitoring
  • Ecosystem resilience
  • Nature-based adaptation measures
  • Monitoring tools and technologies
  • Assessment of environmental adaptation strategies

Topic C: Climate-Driven Water Extremes in Urban Areas

This theme addresses the increasing risks that climate change creates for urban water systems.

Potential research may focus on climate-driven:

  • Flooding
  • Water scarcity
  • Extreme rainfall
  • Urban water challenges
  • Other water-related climate extremes

Researchers investigating how cities can prepare for, manage, and adapt to increasingly severe water-related climate events are encouraged to consider this topic.

Topic D: Sustainable Business Models for Unconventional Water Resources

This research area focuses on developing sustainable approaches for the use and management of unconventional water resources.

Applicants may explore:

  • Sustainable water business models
  • Alternative water resources
  • Economic approaches to water management
  • Resource efficiency
  • Innovative approaches to water supply

The theme highlights the importance of developing solutions that are not only environmentally sustainable but also economically viable.

Topic E: Eco-Friendly Materials and Sustainable Building Solutions for Climate Adaptation

This topic focuses on sustainable materials and construction approaches that can contribute to climate adaptation.

Research may involve:

  • Eco-friendly materials
  • Sustainable building solutions
  • Climate-resilient construction
  • Environmentally sustainable infrastructure
  • Materials that support climate adaptation

Who Can Apply?

The scholarship is specifically designed for doctoral students from developing countries.

Applicants must satisfy the programme’s stated eligibility requirements.

Applicants must:

  • Be doctoral/PhD students.
  • Have commenced their PhD studies within the last three years.
  • Be registered as full-time PhD students.
  • Be enrolled at a university in a developing country.
  • Have a research topic that can be aligned with the thematic areas of the ABCD-Centre.
  • Be able to demonstrate strong academic and research potential.
  • Be prepared to undertake the proposed research stay at the selected German host institution.
  • Have the necessary support and agreement from their home institution and doctoral supervisor.

The call does not specify eligibility according to race or ethnicity. Rather, its geographic eligibility is framed around doctoral students from developing countries/Global South countries who are studying at universities in developing countries.

Applicants should therefore carefully establish that their home country and institution meet the programme’s definition or requirements for developing-country eligibility before submitting an application.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarship provides financial support intended to cover key expenses associated with the research stay in Germany.

The scholarship typically includes support for mobility, accommodation and living expenses, insurance, and travel.

The stated financial components include:

Monthly accommodation and living expenses

Selected scholars will receive:

€1,200 per month

This allowance is intended to contribute towards accommodation and living costs during the research stay.

Insurance allowance

The scholarship provides an insurance allowance of up to:

€105 per month

The exact amount is subject to the programme’s stated maximum.

Travel allowance

A one-time travel expense stipend of up to:

€1,000

is available to support travel expenses associated with the research stay.

Research materials and equipment

In addition to the personal allowances, up to €1,000 may be allocated for research project materials and equipment through the host institution.

This additional funding can provide valuable support for researchers who require specific materials, equipment, or other research-related resources to conduct the approved project.

Duration of the Research Stay

Each scholarship lasts for nine months.

The research stay is scheduled to run from:

March 1, 2027, to November 30, 2027.

Applicants are encouraged to demonstrate their willingness to spend the complete nine-month period in Germany.

Preference is given to candidates who are willing to undertake the full research stay rather than only a shorter period.

Available Host Institutions

Applicants must identify their preferred host institution as part of the application.

RWTH Aachen University

The first option is RWTH Aachen University, located in Aachen, Germany.

Applicants interested in undertaking their proposed research at RWTH Aachen should identify a suitable host scientist and, preferably, obtain an invitation letter from the prospective host.

Technische Universität Dresden

The second option is Technische Universität Dresden (TU Dresden).

Researchers whose projects align with the university’s relevant expertise may select TU Dresden as their preferred host institution.

UNU Resource Nexus

The third option is the UNU Institute for Integrated Management of Material Fluxes and Resources (UNU Resource Nexus), located in Dresden.

This option may be particularly relevant for applicants working on integrated approaches to resources, environmental management, water, sustainability, and related areas.

Application Documents

Applicants are required to compile their application materials into one single PDF file.

The application should contain the following documents:

1. Personal motivation for the research stay

Applicants must provide a 2–3 page motivation statement explaining their motivation for undertaking the research stay.

The statement should clearly communicate why the applicant wants to participate, how the research stay fits into their doctoral project, and how the proposed experience will contribute to their academic and professional development.

2. Sample of a scientific paper

Applicants must provide a sample of a written scientific paper.

This gives the selection committee an opportunity to assess the applicant’s academic writing and research capabilities.

3. Recent Curriculum Vitae

A current CV should be included, highlighting relevant:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Research experience
  • Publications
  • Professional experience
  • Awards
  • Projects
  • Skills
  • Other achievements relevant to the proposed research

4. Preferred host university

Applicants must clearly indicate which of the three participating institutions they prefer:

  • RWTH Aachen University
  • Technische Universität Dresden
  • UNU Resource Nexus

5. Support letter from the home institution

A support letter from the applicant’s home institution is required.

This is important because the research stay forms part of the applicant’s ongoing doctoral work and requires institutional support.

6. Invitation letter from a host scientist

An invitation letter from a prospective host scientist is preferably included.

While the wording indicates that this is preferred rather than listed as an absolute mandatory document, applicants should make every reasonable effort to establish contact with an appropriate host researcher before applying.

7. Statement regarding online work

Applicants must provide a statement demonstrating their ability to work online if remote work is required.

This requirement is relevant to the practical organisation of the research stay and any circumstances in which some research activities may need to be undertaken remotely.

8. Enrollment certificate and transcript

Applicants must submit:

  • An enrollment certificate from their home institution
  • A current transcript of records

These documents must be no older than six months.

9. Passport copy

A copy of the applicant’s passport must also be included in the application.

Agreements Required Before Applying

Before submitting the application, the applicant’s doctoral supervisor and home university must agree on several important aspects of the proposed research stay.

These include the following.

Research topic

The applicant, supervisor, and home institution should agree on a research topic that is aligned with the ABCD-Centre’s research clusters and priorities.

Doctoral project timeline

A detailed timeline of the entire doctoral project must be established.

This should show how the proposed nine-month research stay fits into the applicant’s broader PhD programme.

Research project in Germany

Applicants must describe the specific research project they intend to conduct in Germany.

This description should include:

  • The research objectives
  • Activities to be undertaken
  • A timetable
  • How the research contributes to the overall PhD
  • Plans for future third-party funded research projects

Outreach contributions

Applicants should also describe their planned contributions to the ABCD-Centre’s outreach activities.

This highlights the programme’s emphasis on knowledge sharing and communication beyond the immediate research project.

How Will Applicants Be Selected?

Selection is based on several factors.

The ABCD-Centre’s Steering Committee is responsible for carrying out the selection process.

Key selection considerations include:

Academic merit

Applicants should demonstrate strong academic performance and research potential.

Motivation

The committee will consider the applicant’s motivation to contribute meaningfully to the relevant environmental field.

A strong application should therefore explain not only why the applicant wants to travel to Germany, but also why the proposed research matters and what impact it could have.

Quality of the research proposal

The quality and relevance of the proposed research project are central to the selection process.

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • A clear research problem
  • Well-defined objectives
  • A logical methodology
  • Relevance to the ABCD-Centre
  • Potential practical applications
  • A realistic timeline
  • Potential contribution to policy or practice

Commitment to the full research stay

Preference is given to candidates who are willing to spend the full nine months in Germany.

Policy relevance

Applicants who are interested in translating research findings into policy papers are also given preference.

This reinforces the programme’s objective of connecting academic research with practical environmental and policy solutions.

English proficiency and communication

Proficiency in English is considered important.

Applicants should also demonstrate effective communication skills because the programme involves international academic collaboration, research exchange, and outreach activities.

Adaptability

The ability to adapt to conducting research in Germany is another important consideration.

Successful applicants should be prepared to work within an international research environment and collaborate with researchers from different academic and cultural backgrounds.

Reporting Requirements

Successful scholarship recipients will have responsibilities beyond simply completing their research stay.

Scholarship and experience report

A mandatory scholarship and experience report must be submitted three months before the scholarship ends.

Recipients should therefore keep records throughout the research stay that can help them prepare the required report.

Scientific draft paper

Before the end of the research stay, scholars must submit a scientific draft paper based on the research conducted during the fellowship.

The paper should demonstrate the scientific outcomes of the research stay.

The draft may subsequently be developed further into a publication.

This requirement means that applicants should approach the nine-month stay with a clear plan for generating tangible research outputs.

Rules and Regulations

The scholarship operates under the applicable rules and regulations of:

  • The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD)
  • The German Federal Foreign Office
  • The relevant host institutions

Upon selection, scholarship recipients will be required to sign a contract with their host institution.

The contract will outline the terms of the scholarship and expected conduct during the research stay.

Advice for Prospective Applicants

Applicants should begin preparing well before the deadline because the application requires multiple documents and institutional coordination.

A strong applicant should consider the following steps:

  1. Confirm your eligibility by checking that you are a full-time PhD student at a university in a developing country and that your PhD began within the last three years.
  2. Review the ABCD-Centre research clusters and identify where your doctoral research fits.
  3. Consider the five priority topics and determine whether your project can directly address one of them.
  4. Identify your preferred German host institution based on research fit rather than simply selecting an institution because of its reputation.
  5. Identify potential host scientists whose research interests align with your proposed project.
  6. Seek a host invitation letter early, since the call preferably requests one.
  7. Discuss the proposed research stay with your PhD supervisor and home university and obtain the required institutional support.
  8. Develop a strong research plan showing what you will accomplish during the nine months.
  9. Prepare your motivation statement carefully, explaining the academic, research, practical, and policy value of the proposed stay.
  10. Update your CV and select a strong scientific paper that demonstrates your research and writing ability.
  11. Obtain recent academic documents, making sure the enrollment certificate and transcript are not more than six months old.
  12. Prepare the required statement about online work if remote work becomes necessary.
  13. Ensure all documents are combined into one PDF file before submission.
  14. Submit the application before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarships 2027 is:

October 31, 2026

Applications must be submitted by email to:

abcd-centre@rwth-aachen.de

Applicants should compile all required documents into a single PDF file and send it to the stated email address before the deadline.

Contact and Further Information

For questions concerning the scholarship and application process, applicants can contact the ABCD-Centre directly at:

abcd-centre@rwth-aachen.de

Applicants are also encouraged to seek guidance from their local International Office and DAAD office, particularly regarding questions related to the research stay in Germany.

For more scholarships opportunities visit OFY Website HERE

Why This Scholarship Is a Valuable Opportunity

The ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarship offers more than financial assistance.

For a doctoral researcher from a developing country, a nine-month research stay at a leading German academic or research institution can provide exposure to international research networks, specialised expertise, new methodologies, research infrastructure, and potential future collaborations.

The programme is also strongly focused on translating research into practical solutions. This makes it particularly suitable for researchers who want their work to influence environmental policy, planning, technology, community-level solutions, or sustainable development practices.

The opportunity can also help scholars develop research outputs, international connections, and experience that may support future academic collaborations and third-party research funding.

Conclusion

The ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarships 2027 provide an international research opportunity for doctoral students from developing countries working on important challenges related to water security, climate adaptation, ecosystem resilience, nature-based solutions, sustainable infrastructure, and environmental management.

With two nine-month scholarships available, successful applicants will be able to conduct research at RWTH Aachen University, Technische Universität Dresden, or UNU Resource Nexus in Germany from March 1 to November 30, 2027.

The scholarship provides €1,200 per month for accommodation and living expenses, an insurance allowance of up to €105 per month, a one-time travel stipend of up to €1,000, and potentially up to €1,000 for research materials and equipment through the host institution.

Candidates should pay particular attention to the quality and practical relevance of their research proposal, their motivation, academic record, institutional support, and potential contribution to the ABCD-Centre’s work.

Eligible doctoral students should begin preparing their applications early and submit the complete application as one PDF to abcd-centre@rwth-aachen.de by October 31, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The Department of Quantitative Biomedicine at the University of Zurich (UZH) is inviting applications for a PhD position focused on Medical Imaging AI, offering an opportunity for researchers interested in artificial intelligence, computer vision, medical image computing and clinically relevant machine learning research.

The PhD position is jointly affiliated with the University of Zurich (UZH) and the University Hospital Zurich (USZ), with the possibility of an additional affiliation with the ETH AI Center for an appropriate candidate. The research will also be conducted in active collaboration with the AWS for Healthcare team, giving the successful candidate an opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced AI research, medical imaging and real-world healthcare applications.

The position is particularly relevant to candidates with academic backgrounds in Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, Engineering or closely related disciplines who have a strong interest in medical applications of artificial intelligence and are motivated to develop and scale AI algorithms through the AWS ecosystem.

Host Institutions and Research Environment

The position is hosted by the Department of Quantitative Biomedicine at the University of Zurich and is jointly affiliated with the University Hospital Zurich. The research environment also has strong connections to ETH Zurich, with the possibility for a suitable candidate to affiliate with the ETH AI Center.

A distinctive feature of this opportunity is the collaboration with the AWS for Healthcare team. Rather than focusing solely on theoretical or laboratory-based research, the PhD will combine methodological research with direct clinical relevance and opportunities to translate research outcomes into practical algorithms and applications.

This makes the position particularly attractive for researchers who want to develop expertise not only in artificial intelligence and medical imaging but also in the transition of research innovations into real-world healthcare technology.

Research Areas for the PhD

The PhD position focuses on several interconnected areas of medical imaging artificial intelligence. Applicants should be prepared to engage with advanced computational methods and their application to medical data.

1. Vision-Language Modeling for 3D Medical Imaging

One of the central research directions is vision-language modeling (VLM) for three-dimensional medical imaging.

Vision-language models seek to connect visual information with language-based information. In the context of medical imaging, this can involve developing AI systems capable of understanding complex medical images and relating their visual content to textual descriptions, clinical findings or other forms of medical knowledge.

The position specifically highlights work involving 3D medical imaging, including research associated with CT imaging and the CT-RATE dataset.

This research area has significant potential applications in medical image interpretation, automated reporting, clinical decision support and multimodal healthcare AI.

2. Image Segmentation

Another major research focus is medical image segmentation.

Image segmentation involves identifying and delineating specific structures, organs, tissues, lesions or other clinically relevant regions within medical images.

For a PhD researcher, this area may involve developing machine learning and deep learning approaches that can accurately identify structures within complex medical images and improve the reliability of automated medical image analysis.

The position references research including CADS and vesselFM as part of its segmentation and visual grounding focus.

3. Visual Grounding

The PhD will also address visual grounding, an area concerned with linking language or semantic descriptions to specific regions or objects within visual data.

In medical imaging, visual grounding can contribute to AI systems that do more than simply classify an image. Such systems can potentially identify and associate particular anatomical structures or abnormalities with corresponding clinical concepts or descriptions.

This creates an important connection between computer vision, natural language processing and medical image understanding.

4. Clinical Validation

The research will not stop at developing AI models.

A major component of the position is clinical validation, meaning that developed approaches will need to be assessed for their usefulness and performance in medically relevant settings.

This clinical orientation is one of the defining features of the opportunity. The research will combine methods-driven artificial intelligence research with direct clinical relevance through the UZH and University Hospital Zurich environment.

5. Benchmarking and Public Challenges

The PhD researcher will also have the opportunity to participate in public benchmarking initiatives.

Benchmarking allows researchers to compare AI systems using common datasets, evaluation procedures and performance measures. It can help determine whether a proposed method provides meaningful improvements over existing approaches.

The position specifically references initiatives including VLM3D and BRATS.

Participation in such initiatives can also help researchers build an international research profile and contribute to the broader medical AI research community.

What the PhD Position Offers

The University of Zurich’s opportunity provides an interdisciplinary research environment combining academic research, healthcare and industry collaboration.

According to the official position announcement, successful candidates can benefit from several important opportunities.

1. Research at the Intersection of AI and Medicine

The position combines advanced computational and AI methods with direct clinical applications.

This means the PhD researcher will have the opportunity to investigate sophisticated artificial intelligence methods while considering how those methods can address real healthcare and medical imaging challenges.

2. Affiliation with Leading Swiss Research Institutions

The position is based at UZH and USZ and has strong ties to ETH Zurich.

For an appropriate candidate, there is also the possibility of affiliation with the ETH AI Center, providing an additional connection to Switzerland’s highly developed artificial intelligence research ecosystem.

3. Collaboration with AWS for Healthcare

The successful researcher will work closely with the AWS for Healthcare team and participate in joint activities.

This provides exposure to an industry environment alongside academic and clinical research.

For candidates interested in developing AI systems that can eventually operate at scale, this industry connection may be particularly valuable.

4. Translating Research into Real-World Applications

The PhD offers an opportunity to contribute to the translation of research into real-world algorithms and applications within the AWS ecosystem.

This practical orientation can help bridge the gap between academic research and technology implementation.

5. Access to Clinical Collaborators

The position provides access to clinical collaborators, enabling researchers to work in an environment where medical expertise can inform the development and evaluation of AI systems.

This is especially important in medical AI because successful models need to address real clinical requirements rather than simply perform well on technical datasets.

6. Curated Medical Datasets

The researcher will have access to curated datasets relevant to medical imaging research.

High-quality datasets are essential for developing, training and evaluating machine learning systems, particularly in specialized areas such as 3D medical imaging.

7. Modern Computing Infrastructure

The position also provides access to modern computational infrastructure, including AWS cloud computing resources.

This can be important for computationally intensive research involving large medical imaging datasets and advanced AI models.

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

The position is aimed at candidates with a strong technical and research background relevant to artificial intelligence and medical image computing.

The official announcement identifies the following candidate profile.

Academic Background

Applicants should have a degree in:

  • Computer Science
  • Physics
  • Mathematics
  • Engineering
  • Or a closely related field

The position is therefore particularly suited to graduates whose academic training provides a strong foundation in quantitative, computational or technical research.

Interest in the Medical Domain

An intrinsic interest in the medical domain is required.

The university indicates that this interest should ideally be demonstrated through previous academic work, such as a related Master’s thesis or research project.

Candidates should therefore be able to demonstrate more than a general interest in artificial intelligence. A convincing application should explain why the applicant is interested in applying AI and computational methods to healthcare and medical imaging.

Interest in AWS and Scalable AI

Applicants are also expected to have a genuine interest in working with AWS to establish and scale algorithms and applications through the AWS ecosystem.

Candidates should therefore consider highlighting any relevant experience or interest in areas such as:

  • Machine learning
  • Deep learning
  • Computer vision
  • Medical image analysis
  • Cloud computing
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Data science
  • Algorithm development
  • Research software
  • Scalable computing systems

Who Can Apply?

The official announcement does not specify a particular nationality, race, ethnicity or continent restriction. The listed eligibility requirements focus primarily on academic background, interest in medical research and motivation to work with AWS.

Therefore, based on the published criteria, the opportunity can be considered open to qualified applicants internationally rather than being restricted to applicants from a particular country or continent.

Applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions may be considered provided they satisfy the academic and research requirements. The announcement does not identify a nationality or racial restriction.

However, applicants should rely on the official university announcement for any additional admission, immigration, employment or doctoral-registration requirements that may apply during the application or enrollment process.

Application Requirements

Interested candidates are required to submit three key documents.

1. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants should submit an updated CV highlighting their academic background, research experience, technical skills, projects, publications and other experience relevant to medical AI and computational research.

Where applicable, candidates should emphasize experience with:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Machine learning
  • Deep learning
  • Computer vision
  • Medical imaging
  • Image segmentation
  • Natural language processing
  • Vision-language models
  • Data science
  • Programming
  • Cloud computing
  • Research projects
  • Scientific publications

2. Transcript of Records

Applicants must provide their transcript of records.

The transcript helps demonstrate the candidate’s academic preparation and performance.

Candidates should ensure that the submitted transcript is clear and readable and adequately reflects their relevant academic coursework.

3. Brief Statement of Motivation

Applicants must also submit a brief statement of motivation.

This document should explain why the candidate is interested in the PhD position and why their academic and research background makes them suitable for the project.

A strong motivation statement should connect three major elements:

  1. Your academic and technical background
  2. Your interest in medical imaging and AI
  3. Your motivation to work with UZH, USZ and AWS

Rather than simply stating that you are interested in artificial intelligence, the statement should demonstrate how your previous studies, research projects or technical experience have prepared you for the proposed research area.

How to Apply

Applications should be sent directly by email to:

bjoern.menze@uzh.ch

Applicants should include:

  • CV
  • Transcript of records
  • Brief statement of motivation

The email subject line should clearly state:

“PhD Position UZH-AWS”

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

The official UZH webpage currently states the deadline as 31 September 2026.

However, September has only 30 days, meaning 31 September is not a valid calendar date. In addition, a recent post by the research group supervisor, Prof. Bjoern Menze, has publicly indicated 30 September 2026 as the deadline.

Applicants should therefore treat 30 September 2026 as the likely intended deadline and, importantly, confirm the deadline directly with UZH before submitting.

Because the official university webpage itself contains the apparent date error, applicants should avoid waiting until the final day and should submit their applications as early as possible.

How to Make Your Application Competitive

This is a specialized PhD opportunity, so applicants should carefully demonstrate their suitability rather than submitting a generic doctoral application.

1. Demonstrate Technical Preparation

Show evidence of your ability to work with quantitative and computational research.

Relevant coursework, research projects, programming experience and technical projects can strengthen your application.

2. Connect Your Experience to Medical Imaging

If you have previously worked on medical imaging, biomedical engineering, healthcare AI, computer vision or related research, make this connection explicit.

If your background is primarily in computer science or another technical discipline, explain clearly how you intend to apply your existing expertise to medical research.

3. Explain Your Interest in AI for Healthcare

The project is not simply an AI research position. It is specifically concerned with medical imaging AI.

Your motivation statement should therefore explain why you want to work on healthcare applications and what makes this research area particularly meaningful to you.

4. Highlight Research Experience

Where applicable, mention:

  • Master’s research
  • Research assistant positions
  • Academic publications
  • Conference presentations
  • Machine learning projects
  • Computer vision projects
  • Medical research projects
  • Open-source contributions
  • Relevant software or technical projects

5. Demonstrate Interest in Industry Collaboration

Because the PhD involves close collaboration with AWS for Healthcare, applicants should demonstrate that they are interested in translating research into practical applications.

Experience working with industry, cloud technologies, applied AI projects or scalable computational systems can therefore be useful to highlight.

6. Explain Your Long-Term Research Goals

A strong application should demonstrate how the PhD fits into your broader research and professional ambitions.

For example, candidates may explain their interest in developing AI systems that can improve medical image interpretation, clinical decision-making, healthcare efficiency or biomedical research.

Why This PhD Opportunity Stands Out

The UZH-AWS PhD position brings together four important components that are increasingly influential in modern healthcare research:

Artificial Intelligence + Medical Imaging + Clinical Research + Cloud Technology

The combination provides a distinctive research environment.

Instead of developing AI models in isolation, researchers will have opportunities to work with clinical collaborators, medical datasets and industry partners while investigating advanced approaches such as vision-language modeling, segmentation and visual grounding.

The position also provides exposure to benchmarking and clinical validation, allowing research outcomes to be evaluated against established standards and potentially translated into practical healthcare applications.

Visit HERE for more information about the PhD Position in Medical Imaging AI at the University of Zurich and AWS.

Key Details at a Glance

  • Opportunity: PhD Position in Medical Imaging AI
  • Host: University of Zurich
  • Clinical affiliation: University Hospital Zurich
  • Potential additional affiliation: ETH AI Center
  • Industry collaborator: AWS for Healthcare
  • Location: Zurich, Switzerland
  • Research area: Medical image computing and artificial intelligence
  • Major research topics: 3D vision-language modeling, image segmentation, visual grounding, clinical validation and benchmarking
  • Eligible academic backgrounds: Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, Engineering and closely related disciplines
  • Medical interest: Required
  • AWS interest: Required
  • Application documents: CV, transcript of records and brief motivation statement
  • Application method: Email
  • Application email: bjoern.menze@uzh.ch
  • Required subject line: “PhD Position UZH-AWS”
  • Deadline stated on official page: 31 September 2026, which is an invalid calendar date
  • Likely intended deadline: 30 September 2026, based on the research group’s public announcement
  • Nationality restriction: None stated in the published eligibility criteria
  • Opportunity category: PhD Position / Doctoral Research Opportunity

Conclusion

The PhD Position UZH-AWS in Medical Imaging AI offers an opportunity for technically trained researchers to pursue doctoral research at the intersection of artificial intelligence, medical imaging and healthcare.

With research spanning 3D vision-language modeling, image segmentation, visual grounding, clinical validation and benchmarking, the project is designed for candidates who want to tackle challenging problems in medical image computing while maintaining a strong connection to real-world clinical applications.

The collaboration between the University of Zurich, University Hospital Zurich and AWS for Healthcare, together with potential links to the ETH AI Center, creates a multidisciplinary environment in which doctoral research can connect academic innovation with practical healthcare technology.

Applicants with backgrounds in Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, Engineering or related disciplines should carefully assess their academic preparation, research interests and motivation for working in medical AI before applying.

For more global PhD opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Women entrepreneurs, aspiring business owners, nonprofit founders, and community changemakers around the world can now apply for the Giving Joy Grant 2026. The initiative provides microgrants of up to $500 USD to support innovative ideas that create meaningful economic and social benefits for women, girls, families, and communities.

Giving Joy receives thousands of applications during each grant cycle, making the program highly competitive. However, the organization emphasizes that applicants do not need polished proposals or sophisticated business plans to stand out. Instead, successful applications are expected to demonstrate practical ideas, creativity, initiative, feasibility, and a clear potential for community impact.

Beginning in 2026, Giving Joy has introduced a simplified global grant model with two grant cycles per year. Unlike previous regional rounds, each cycle is now open to eligible women entrepreneurs and changemakers from anywhere in the world.

The Fall 2026 Giving Joy Microgrant Round opened on September 1, 2026, offering women globally an opportunity to secure funding to start or expand businesses, nonprofit organizations, NGOs, charities, projects, and other initiatives focused on improving the lives of women, girls, families, and communities.

About the Giving Joy Grant

Giving Joy is an organization committed to supporting women entrepreneurs and empowering women to transform innovative ideas into initiatives that generate meaningful social and economic impact.

The Giving Joy Grant provides financial support to women who have practical and creative ideas but may lack the resources needed to take the next step. The funding can support a wide range of initiatives, provided they are legal and demonstrate benefits beyond individual financial gain.

Applicants are encouraged to think broadly about how their ideas can contribute to positive change. A proposal may involve launching a new business, expanding an existing enterprise, establishing a nonprofit organization, implementing a community project, delivering skills training, or developing an innovative initiative that benefits women and families.

The program is particularly interested in projects that create multiplied impact. This means that successful proposals should demonstrate how a relatively small amount of funding can create benefits that extend beyond the applicant herself.

For example, a woman may use the grant to organize skills training for unemployed women, establish a community-based initiative that creates income opportunities, conduct educational workshops, or develop a project that improves access to knowledge, leadership opportunities, safety, or economic independence.

Giving Joy Grant 2026 Funding Amount

Successful applicants may receive grants of up to $500 USD.

The exact amount awarded may be determined by Giving Joy based on several factors, including:

  • The proposed activities.
  • The applicant’s project budget.
  • The feasibility of the proposal.
  • The potential social and economic impact.
  • The availability of funding.
  • How effectively the proposed grant amount will support the initiative.

Applicants should therefore provide a clear and realistic explanation of how they intend to use the requested funding.

A strong application should not simply state that the applicant needs money for a business or project. Instead, applicants should clearly demonstrate exactly how the funding will be spent and what outcomes are expected.

For instance, applicants may need to explain:

  • What materials they intend to purchase.
  • What activities they plan to organize.
  • Who will participate.
  • How many people are expected to benefit.
  • What the estimated costs will be.
  • How the grant will contribute to long-term impact.

2026 Giving Joy Grant Cycle

Beginning in 2026, Giving Joy has moved to a new grant structure consisting of two global grant cycles each year.

The organization previously conducted multiple regional grant rounds. However, after reviewing feedback from applicants and volunteer reviewers, Giving Joy determined that operating four cycles created unnecessary administrative complexity.

The new approach is designed to create a simpler, more transparent, and more effective application process.

According to the organization, the new structure will help:

  • Provide clearer timelines for applicants.
  • Improve the quality and depth of application reviews.
  • Reduce administrative burdens.
  • Allow the organization to provide better support to grant recipients.
  • Improve communication and fundraising efforts.
  • Ensure women entrepreneurs from all regions have access to the same global application opportunities.

Most importantly, each cycle is open to eligible women entrepreneurs and changemakers worldwide without dividing applicants into regional categories.

Giving Joy Grant 2026 Timeline

Cycle 1 – Spring 2026

The first Giving Joy Grant Cycle for 2026 has already closed.

The timeline was as follows:

  • Applications opened: April 1, 2026.
  • Application deadline: April 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST.
  • Awards announced: August 2026.

The Spring 2026 round attracted significant global interest, receiving 6,423 applications from women entrepreneurs around the world.

Despite the extremely competitive application pool, Giving Joy awarded 10 microgrants during the cycle.

This demonstrates both the global popularity of the program and the importance of submitting a clear, specific, and impactful application.

Cycle 2 – Fall 2026 Giving Joy Microgrant Round

The second and current Giving Joy Grant Cycle for 2026 opened in September.

The Fall 2026 Microgrant Round follows the schedule below:

  • Applications open: September 1, 2026.
  • Application deadline: September 30, 2026.
  • Review period: October 1 to November 30, 2026.
  • Shortlisted applicants notified: During the review period.
  • Unsuccessful application notification: Applicants who have not heard from Giving Joy by December 1 should consider their applications unsuccessful.
  • Awards announced: Beginning of December 2026.

Giving Joy Grant 2026 Deadline

The deadline to apply for the Fall 2026 Giving Joy Microgrant Round is:

September 30, 2026.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications. Given the high number of applications received during each grant cycle, it is important to carefully complete all sections of the online application form and ensure that the proposed project is clearly explained.

Who Can Apply for the Giving Joy Grant?

The Giving Joy Grant is designed to support women aged 18 years and above.

One of the major strengths of the program is its global accessibility. Applicants are not restricted to specific countries, regions, continents, or territories.

Eligible women can apply from anywhere in the world.

Applicants may include women who want to:

  • Start a new business.
  • Expand an existing business.
  • Launch a nonprofit organization.
  • Develop an NGO initiative.
  • Establish a charity project.
  • Implement a community-based initiative.
  • Organize a training program.
  • Create employment opportunities.
  • Develop an innovative social enterprise.
  • Implement a specific activity benefiting women or families.

Applicants do not necessarily need to own an existing business before applying.

This means that women with innovative ideas who are still at the planning stage can also submit applications.

What Types of Projects Can Be Funded?

Giving Joy does not limit applications to a specific industry, professional sector, trade, occupation, or craft.

Applicants can propose projects from a wide range of fields.

However, the proposed business, organization, project, or initiative should demonstrate clear benefits for women, girls, families, or communities.

Potential areas may include:

  • Women’s entrepreneurship.
  • Skills development.
  • Vocational training.
  • Community development.
  • Education.
  • Social enterprises.
  • Employment creation.
  • Women’s leadership.
  • Economic empowerment.
  • Legal awareness.
  • Community workshops.
  • Professional training.
  • Creative enterprises.
  • Agriculture.
  • Technology initiatives.
  • Crafts and trades.
  • Environmental projects.
  • Family support initiatives.

All proposed activities must be legal.

Giving Joy is particularly interested in projects that create opportunities beyond the applicant’s individual financial interests.

For example, a business that creates employment or training opportunities for other women may demonstrate stronger community impact than a proposal focused solely on personal income.

What Giving Joy Looks for in Grant Applications

Giving Joy evaluates applications based on several important criteria.

Applicants should carefully consider these factors when developing their proposals.

1. Alignment With Giving Joy’s Mission

The proposed initiative should support the broader mission of empowering and inspiring women.

Projects should ideally contribute to areas such as:

  • Women’s leadership.
  • Economic independence.
  • Dignity.
  • Opportunity creation.
  • Entrepreneurship.
  • Community empowerment.

Applicants should demonstrate how their idea contributes to positive outcomes for women and their communities.

2. Social and Economic Impact

Giving Joy places significant emphasis on projects that can create meaningful benefits.

A strong application should explain how the proposed activities will positively affect:

  • Women.
  • Girls.
  • Families.
  • Communities.

Applicants should clearly identify the people who will benefit and explain the expected outcomes.

For example, rather than simply stating that a project will empower women, applicants should provide specific details about what empowerment will look like in practice.

This could include:

  • Training 20 women in a professional skill.
  • Creating income opportunities for mothers.
  • Providing educational workshops.
  • Supporting women to understand their legal rights.
  • Establishing a community enterprise.
  • Creating employment opportunities.
  • Developing leadership programs.

Specific and measurable impact is generally more compelling than broad statements.

3. Innovation and Creativity

Giving Joy prioritizes creative and innovative ideas.

Applicants are encouraged to propose approaches that address genuine challenges faced by women and communities.

Innovation does not necessarily mean using advanced technology or creating something that has never existed before.

Instead, applicants can demonstrate innovation by:

  • Developing a creative solution to a local problem.
  • Combining existing approaches in a new way.
  • Creating a practical community-based model.
  • Identifying an overlooked challenge.
  • Designing an initiative with multiplied benefits.

The key is to demonstrate initiative and thoughtful problem-solving.

4. Effective Use of the $500 Grant

Applicants must explain how the grant funds will be used.

Giving Joy expects applicants to provide a practical and specific budget.

A strong budget should identify:

  • The materials or resources required.
  • Estimated costs.
  • Planned activities.
  • Expected outputs.
  • Number of beneficiaries.

Applicants should avoid vague statements such as “the money will help grow my business.”

Instead, they should provide concrete information.

For example:

  • Purchase training materials for a vocational workshop.
  • Rent a venue for community training sessions.
  • Purchase equipment necessary to provide a service.
  • Develop educational resources.
  • Support the implementation of a specific community activity.

The proposed use of funds should be realistic within the $500 funding limit.

5. Clarity and Feasibility

The application should be easy to understand.

Applicants do not need to use complicated language or highly polished writing.

Giving Joy specifically emphasizes that practical ideas and real community impact are more important than sophisticated writing.

However, the application should clearly explain:

  1. What the applicant intends to do.
  2. Why the project is needed.
  3. Who will benefit.
  4. How the grant will be used.
  5. What outcomes are expected.

The proposal should also be realistic and achievable within the six-month grant period.

How to Write a Strong Giving Joy Grant Application

Given the high number of applications received during each grant cycle, applicants should take time to develop clear responses.

Here are some important strategies for preparing a competitive application.

Be Specific About Your Project

Avoid general statements.

Clearly explain what you plan to do and how you intend to implement the activities.

For example, instead of saying:

” I want to empower women through training.”

Explain:

” I plan to organize a practical skills training program for 15 unemployed women in my community, focusing on a specific skill that can help participants generate income.”

Specific proposals help reviewers understand the project and evaluate its feasibility.

Clearly Identify the Beneficiaries

Explain exactly who will benefit from the project.

Consider questions such as:

  • Are the beneficiaries unemployed women?
  • Young women?
  • Mothers?
  • Girls?
  • Rural communities?
  • Women entrepreneurs?
  • Families facing economic challenges?

Also explain approximately how many people will benefit.

Demonstrate Community Impact

Giving Joy is interested in projects that create benefits beyond personal business growth.

Applicants should explain how the initiative can generate wider social or economic impact.

For example, an applicant might propose:

  • Training 10 women in construction skills.
  • Providing legal education workshops for 20 women.
  • Establishing a community initiative that creates income opportunities.
  • Creating skills programs that enable participants to support their families.

The stronger the explanation of multiplied impact, the stronger the proposal may be.

Develop a Clear Budget

Applicants should show exactly how they plan to spend the funding.

A simple budget may include:

  • Equipment or materials.
  • Training resources.
  • Venue costs.
  • Transportation directly related to project activities.
  • Implementation costs.

Every expense should connect directly to the proposed project.

Focus on Practical Impact

Giving Joy values real-world outcomes.

Applicants should therefore focus on practical questions such as:

  • What problem does the project solve?
  • Who experiences the problem?
  • What activities will address it?
  • What changes will happen after implementation?
  • How many people will benefit?

A proposal that clearly answers these questions will be easier for reviewers to evaluate.

Activities Giving Joy Does Not Primarily Fund

Applicants should carefully review the restrictions before submitting their applications.

Giving Joy indicates that it does not primarily fund activities focused mainly on:

  • Purchasing merchandise or inventory for resale.
  • Advertising.
  • Marketing activities.
  • Personal expenses that are not connected to broader community impact.

This does not mean applicants cannot propose business-related ideas.

However, the proposal should demonstrate that the funding will contribute to wider economic or social benefits rather than simply supporting individual commercial activities.

Applicants should therefore carefully explain the community value of their projects.

Grant Duration

Successful applicants will have up to six months to implement their proposed projects.

The six-month grant period gives recipients time to organize activities, use the awarded funds, and deliver the proposed outcomes.

Applicants should therefore develop projects that can realistically be implemented within this timeframe.

When planning an application, it may be helpful to create a simple implementation schedule covering:

  1. Project preparation.
  2. Purchase of necessary materials.
  3. Participant identification.
  4. Activity implementation.
  5. Community engagement.
  6. Monitoring of outcomes.
  7. Completion of project deliverables.

A realistic implementation plan can demonstrate that the applicant has carefully considered how the project will move from idea to execution.

Can Applicants Apply in Languages Other Than English?

Yes.

Giving Joy accepts applications in any language that can be translated using Google Translate.

This significantly improves accessibility for women entrepreneurs and changemakers from different linguistic backgrounds.

Applicants should still ensure that their responses are clear and understandable.

Simple and direct language may be particularly useful because the organization emphasizes that clear, practical ideas are more important than polished writing.

How Does the Giving Joy Application Process Work?

The Giving Joy application process involves several stages.

Step 1: Submit the Online Application

Applications must be submitted online through the official application platform.

Giving Joy does not accept proposals or funding requests submitted through email.

Applicants must therefore use the designated online application form.

Step 2: Application Compliance Review

After submission, Giving Joy reviews applications to ensure they meet the basic requirements.

The organization may contact applicants if additional information or clarification is needed.

Applicants may also be asked to provide supporting information, including photos of themselves or their businesses or organizations.

Step 3: Application Evaluation

Giving Joy staff evaluate eligible applications based on criteria such as:

  • Alignment with the organization’s mission.
  • Innovative use of grant funding.
  • Social and economic impact.
  • Community benefits.
  • Feasibility.
  • Clarity of the proposed activities.

Step 4: Shortlisting

Based on the evaluation process, Giving Joy may shortlist approximately 10 applications per grant round.

Due to the large number of applications received, the organization only contacts shortlisted applicants.

Step 5: Final Evaluation

Giving Joy Board Members evaluate shortlisted applicants using similar assessment criteria.

Board members may contact applicants to request additional information or clarification.

Step 6: Grant Notification

Successful applicants are notified individually via email.

If an applicant does not receive communication from Giving Joy within the stated notification period, the application should be considered unsuccessful.

For the Fall 2026 cycle, applicants who have not heard from Giving Joy by December 1, 2026, should consider their applications unsuccessful.

Step 7: Grant Agreement and Project Implementation

Successful applicants will participate in discussions with Giving Joy regarding:

  • Grant terms and conditions.
  • Project deliverables.
  • Implementation guidelines.
  • Grant agreement requirements.

Once the grant agreement is signed, recipients will have up to six months to implement their proposed projects.

Can You Apply More Than Once?

Applicants can only submit one application per grant cycle.

Women who are unsuccessful may apply again during future grant cycles.

However, applicants who have already received a Giving Joy grant cannot apply again.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they submit their strongest possible proposal during each application cycle.

What Happens if You Win the Giving Joy Grant?

Successful applicants may receive funding of up to $500 USD.

The award amount will depend on:

  • The proposed activities.
  • The project’s financial requirements.
  • The availability of funding.
  • Giving Joy’s funding decision.

Successful grantees will also receive guidance regarding grant implementation requirements.

Recipients will need to review and sign a grant agreement before beginning implementation.

The organization will then expect grantees to implement their proposed activities within the designated six-month period.

Why the Giving Joy Grant Is a Valuable Opportunity

The Giving Joy Grant is particularly valuable because it provides accessible microfunding to women with ideas that may otherwise struggle to secure traditional investment or large grants.

Many funding opportunities require applicants to have established organizations, extensive financial records, or complex proposals.

Giving Joy offers a different approach by emphasizing initiative, creativity, practical planning, and community impact.

Key advantages of the program include:

  • Funding of up to $500 USD.
  • Open to women worldwide.
  • Applicants do not need to own an existing business.
  • Supports businesses, nonprofits, NGOs, charities, and community projects.
  • No restriction to a specific professional field.
  • Applications accepted in multiple languages.
  • Focus on innovative and creative ideas.
  • Six months available for project implementation.
  • Opportunity to create social and economic impact.
  • Accessible online application process.

Although the funding amount is relatively modest, the program recognizes that small amounts of capital can create significant change when used strategically.

Important Tips Before Applying

Before submitting your Giving Joy Grant application, consider the following checklist:

  • Confirm that you are eligible to apply.
  • Ensure you are applying only once during the current cycle.
  • Complete every section of the application form.
  • Clearly explain your proposed project.
  • Identify the women, girls, families, or communities who will benefit.
  • Explain the social and economic impact.
  • Provide a realistic budget.
  • Show exactly how the grant funds will be used.
  • Demonstrate creativity and initiative.
  • Ensure your project is legal.
  • Avoid proposals focused primarily on inventory resale, advertising, marketing, or unrelated personal expenses.
  • Ensure your project can be implemented within six months.
  • Submit your application before the deadline.
  • Keep your project description practical and easy to understand.

APPLY HERE

How to Apply for the Giving Joy Grant 2026

Interested applicants must submit their applications online through the official Giving Joy Microgrant application form.

Email applications and funding proposals are not accepted.

Applicants should carefully review the application questions and provide complete, specific, and practical answers.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Giving Joy Grant 2026.

Conclusion

The Giving Joy Grant 2026 presents an important funding opportunity for women entrepreneurs, aspiring business owners, nonprofit founders, and community changemakers who have innovative ideas capable of creating meaningful social or economic impact.

With grants of up to $500 USD, the program supports initiatives that go beyond individual financial growth and demonstrate clear benefits for women, girls, families, and communities. The opportunity is particularly accessible because applicants do not need to own an existing business, proposals can come from any legal field, and women from countries around the world are eligible to apply.

However, competition is expected to be intense. Giving Joy receives thousands of applications during each grant cycle and awards only a limited number of microgrants. Applicants should therefore focus on presenting a clear, specific, creative, and practical project with measurable community benefits.

For the Fall 2026 cycle, eligible applicants should submit their online applications by September 30, 2026, and ensure that their proposals clearly demonstrate how the funding will create meaningful and lasting impact.
