item.content:encoded:
The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) 2027/28 is now accepting applications from outstanding prospective doctoral students from around the world who want to pursue full-time PhD studies at participating universities in Hong Kong.

Established by Hong Kong’s Research Grants Council (RGC) in 2009, the scheme was created to attract high-achieving researchers and talented doctoral students from around the world to Hong Kong’s universities. The programme is open to applicants regardless of their country of origin, prior work experience or ethnic background, making it a genuinely international doctoral fellowship opportunity.

For the 2027/28 academic year, the scheme will award 400 PhD fellowships. The current official scheme information lists an annual fellowship stipend of HK$344,400, together with an annual HK$14,400 conference and research-related travel allowance, with fellowship support provided for up to three years.

The application period for the 2027/28 intake runs from 1 September 2026 to 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time. Late initial applications will not be considered.

What Is the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme?

The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme is a competitive doctoral fellowship programme established by the Research Grants Council to attract talented researchers to Hong Kong.

The scheme supports students seeking admission as new full-time PhD students at participating Hong Kong universities.

Rather than restricting applications to applicants from a particular country or region, the scheme is designed to attract talented doctoral candidates internationally.

The programme is therefore relevant to prospective PhD students from:

  • Africa
  • Asia
  • Europe
  • North America
  • South America
  • Oceania
  • Other regions around the world

The official eligibility information states that applicants are considered irrespective of their country of origin, prior work experience and ethnic background.

What Makes the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme Special?

One of the major attractions of the HKPFS is the level of financial support available to successful fellows.

For the current fellowship information published by the Research Grants Council, each awardee receives:

  • HK$344,400 per year in fellowship stipend.
  • HK$14,400 per year for conference and research-related travel.
  • Fellowship support for up to three years.
  • Potential additional support from the chosen university if the PhD requires more than three years to complete.

For the 2027/28 academic year, 400 PhD fellowships will be awarded. Hong Kong universities normally begin their academic year in September.

The travel allowance is particularly valuable for doctoral researchers who need to attend academic conferences, present research findings or undertake research-related travel.

Who Can Apply for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship?

The scheme is open to individuals seeking admission as new full-time PhD students at one of the participating Hong Kong universities.

Applicants can come from any country or region, and the scheme does not restrict eligibility based on ethnic background or previous work experience.

However, applicants must satisfy the admission requirements of the university and specific PhD programme they choose.

In addition to meeting university admission requirements, applicants should demonstrate strong qualities in several areas.

These include:

  1. Outstanding academic performance
  2. Research ability or potential
  3. Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  4. Excellent leadership abilities

These characteristics form an important part of the fellowship’s selection process.

Academic Excellence Is a Major Selection Factor

The HKPFS selection process places particular emphasis on academic excellence.

However, academic results are not the only factor considered.

The selection panels also assess:

  • Research ability and potential.
  • Communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Leadership abilities.

This means that applicants should present themselves as well-rounded researchers rather than relying exclusively on academic grades.

A strong application should demonstrate both academic achievement and evidence that the applicant has the potential to become an independent and impactful researcher.

Research Ability and Potential

Research capability is another major component of the selection process.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate their potential to undertake doctoral-level research successfully.

This may be reflected through:

  • Previous research projects.
  • Undergraduate or master’s research.
  • Research publications.
  • Conference presentations.
  • Research-related work experience.
  • A well-developed proposed research direction.
  • Evidence of analytical and problem-solving abilities.

The selection process considers not only what applicants have already achieved but also their potential for future research.

Communication and Interpersonal Skills

The fellowship also considers communication and interpersonal skills.

Doctoral researchers frequently work with supervisors, research teams, academic institutions and researchers from different countries.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate that they can:

  • Communicate research ideas clearly.
  • Work effectively with others.
  • Participate in academic discussions.
  • Build professional relationships.
  • Present ideas to different audiences.

Leadership Abilities

Leadership is also one of the four major criteria used in the HKPFS assessment.

Applicants should consider how their academic, professional, research or community experiences demonstrate leadership potential.

Leadership does not necessarily mean holding a formal leadership position. Evidence of taking initiative, leading projects, contributing to research teams or creating meaningful academic or community impact can help demonstrate leadership potential.

Participating Universities

Applicants can apply for PhD programmes at the following eight participating universities:

1. City University of Hong Kong

City University of Hong Kong is one of the participating institutions where HKPFS applicants can pursue eligible doctoral programmes.

2. Hong Kong Baptist University

Hong Kong Baptist University is another participating university offering doctoral study opportunities under the scheme.

3. Lingnan University

Lingnan University is included among the eight participating institutions.

4. The Chinese University of Hong Kong

The Chinese University of Hong Kong participates in the HKPFS and offers doctoral programmes across a broad range of disciplines.

5. The Education University of Hong Kong

The Education University of Hong Kong is also part of the participating university network.

6. The Hong Kong Polytechnic University

The Hong Kong Polytechnic University participates in the scheme and provides PhD opportunities across multiple academic and research areas.

7. The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology is another participating institution.

8. The University of Hong Kong

The University of Hong Kong, one of the region’s major research universities, is also included in the scheme.

The Research Grants Council confirms that applicants can seek admission as new full-time PhD students at these eight universities.

How Many Universities Can You Apply To?

Applicants may choose a maximum of two programmes within one or two participating universities for their PhD study.

This means applicants should carefully research their preferred programmes before completing the initial HKPFS application.

Candidates should consider:

  • The university’s research strengths.
  • The specific PhD programme.
  • Potential supervisors.
  • Research facilities.
  • Programme requirements.
  • University-specific application deadlines.
  • The suitability of the programme for their proposed research.

HKPFS Application Process

Applying for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme involves more than completing the initial fellowship application.

Applicants must complete the HKPFS initial application and also submit full PhD admission applications to their selected universities.

Step 1: Identify Your Preferred PhD Programme

Applicants should first identify suitable PhD programmes at the participating universities.

Research the programmes carefully and ensure that you meet their specific admission requirements.

Step 2: Submit the HKPFS Initial Application

The initial application is submitted through the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme Electronic System (HKPFSES).

For the 2027/28 intake, the application system is open from:

1 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time

until:

1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time.

Step 3: Obtain Your HKPFS Reference Number

After submitting the initial application, applicants receive an HKPFS Reference Number.

This reference number is important because applicants must use it when communicating with the RGC and when submitting applications to their selected universities.

Applicants should save the confirmation email containing their reference number and login information.

Step 4: Submit Full Applications to the Universities

Completing the HKPFS initial application is not enough.

Applicants must also submit a full PhD admission application to the university or universities selected in their initial application.

The university applications must be submitted before the individual universities’ own deadlines.

The universities may have different application deadlines, so candidates should check each institution carefully.

An initial HKPFS application that is not followed by the required university application will be considered void and will not be processed further by the RGC.

University Admission Requirements Still Apply

Applicants should understand that receiving an HKPFS fellowship is separate from satisfying the admission requirements of the selected university and PhD programme.

Candidates must comply with the relevant university’s:

  • PhD admission requirements.
  • Application procedures.
  • Programme requirements.
  • Application deadlines.
  • Other applicable university regulations and policies.

Universities will normally conduct interviews as part of their assessment process.

Selection Panels

Shortlisted applications are assessed according to the applicant’s area of study.

The scheme has two major selection panels:

Sciences, Medicine, Engineering and Technology

This panel considers applications relating to scientific, medical, engineering and technological areas.

Humanities, Social Sciences and Business Studies

This panel considers research in humanities, social sciences and business-related areas.

The panels consist of experts in the relevant areas.

How Applicants Are Assessed

The four main selection criteria are:

1. Academic Excellence

The academic record of the applicant is a primary consideration.

Candidates should demonstrate strong academic performance and the ability to succeed at doctoral level.

2. Research Ability and Potential

Applicants should demonstrate their capacity and potential to conduct high-quality research.

3. Communication and Interpersonal Skills

The panels assess whether candidates can communicate effectively and work successfully with others.

4. Leadership Abilities

Applicants should demonstrate leadership potential through their academic, professional, research or other relevant experiences.

The RGC states that academic excellence is the prime consideration, while the other three areas are also taken into account.

What Happens If You Are Not Selected for the Fellowship?

Not being selected for the HKPFS fellowship does not necessarily mean that the applicant cannot pursue a PhD in Hong Kong.

Candidates who are not selected for the fellowship may still be accepted by the university for regular PhD admission.

In some cases, universities may offer successful university applicants a postgraduate studentship or other financial support.

Therefore, applicants should still submit their university applications even though fellowship selection is competitive.

Application Fee

The Research Grants Council does not charge an application fee for the HKPFS.

However, individual universities may charge their own application or processing fees.

Applicants should therefore check the fee requirements of each university to which they apply.

Important Application Rule: Submit Only One Initial HKPFS Application

Applicants should be particularly careful about the number of initial HKPFS applications they submit.

Only one initial application is accepted per applicant.

Submitting multiple initial applications can result in disqualification of all applications, even if a university subsequently nominates the applicant for the fellowship.

Applicants who accidentally submit multiple applications are advised to contact the RGC immediately before the application deadline.

Application Language

The initial HKPFS application must be completed in English, except for the field requiring an applicant’s name in Chinese where applicable.

Applicants should therefore ensure that the information provided in the initial application is clear, accurate and consistent.

Keep Your Information Consistent

The RGC cross-checks information submitted through the HKPFS system with information provided in university applications.

Applicants should therefore ensure that:

  • Personal information is accurate.
  • Academic information is consistent.
  • Research information is consistent.
  • University choices match the initial application.
  • Programme information is correct.
  • Supporting information does not conflict between applications.

Inconsistencies or incomplete information may result in an application not being considered.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28 is:

1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time (HKT).

The application period begins on 1 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time.

Late initial applications will not be considered.

Applicants should also remember that the universities have their own application deadlines, which may differ from the HKPFS deadline.

Important Dates

Event Date
Application opens 1 September 2026
Application opening time 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time
Application deadline 1 December 2026
Application deadline time 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time
Academic year 2027/28
Number of fellowships 400

The RGC’s current announcement confirms that the 2027/28 application round opened on 1 September 2026 and closes on 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time.

Fellowship Duration and Additional Support

The fellowship provides the stated annual stipend and research-related travel allowance for up to three years.

If an awardee needs more than three years to complete the PhD, additional support may be available from the university where the student is enrolled.

Applicants requiring additional support should contact their chosen university directly for information about its policies and funding arrangements.

Expected Academic Experience

The HKPFS is intended for students who want to undertake full-time doctoral research in Hong Kong.

Successful fellows will become part of the research communities at their selected universities and pursue doctoral research under the academic supervision and requirements of their chosen programme.

The participating universities cover a wide range of disciplines, allowing applicants from different academic backgrounds to explore doctoral opportunities across areas such as:

  • Humanities
  • Social sciences
  • Business
  • Engineering
  • Technology
  • Medicine
  • Science
  • Other research disciplines offered by participating institutions

The precise programmes available under the fellowship depend on the participating universities and their individual PhD offerings.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The HKPFS may be particularly suitable for students who:

  • Want to pursue a full-time PhD in Hong Kong.
  • Have an excellent academic record.
  • Have strong research potential.
  • Want to develop an international research career.
  • Have strong communication and interpersonal abilities.
  • Have demonstrated leadership potential.
  • Are prepared to meet university-specific PhD admission requirements.
  • Can identify suitable research programmes at participating universities.

The scheme is particularly competitive, so applicants should carefully develop their academic and research profiles before applying.

Preparing a Competitive Application

Although the RGC identifies academic excellence as the primary consideration, applicants should also pay close attention to the other three assessment areas.

A strong candidate should aim to demonstrate:

Strong Academic Performance

Your academic record should show your ability to perform successfully at postgraduate level.

Clear Research Potential

Your research background and proposed doctoral direction should demonstrate your potential to conduct meaningful and high-quality research.

Strong Communication

Your application should communicate your academic interests and research goals clearly.

Leadership Potential

Your academic, professional, community or research experiences should demonstrate initiative and leadership potential where applicable.

What Applicants Should Do Before the Deadline

Prospective applicants should avoid waiting until the final day of the application period.

A practical preparation process would be to:

  1. Research the eight participating universities.
  2. Identify suitable PhD programmes.
  3. Review programme-specific admission requirements.
  4. Identify potential supervisors where appropriate.
  5. Review university application deadlines.
  6. Prepare academic and research information.
  7. Complete the HKPFS initial application.
  8. Record and save the HKPFS Reference Number.
  9. Submit full applications to the selected universities.
  10. Check that all information is accurate and consistent.
  11. Confirm that applications are submitted before the relevant deadlines.

Official Application Information

Applicants should use the official Research Grants Council information when preparing their applications.

The official HKPFS 2027/28 application system is available through the Research Grants Council’s electronic application platform.

Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme official application information

Applicants should also check the individual university websites for programme-specific admission requirements and deadlines.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28

Conclusion

The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28 is a major international doctoral fellowship opportunity for high-achieving students seeking to pursue full-time PhD studies at participating universities in Hong Kong.

The scheme will provide 400 fellowships for the 2027/28 academic year, while the current official fellowship information lists an annual stipend of HK$344,400 and an additional HK$14,400 annual allowance for conference and research-related travel, for up to three years.

The opportunity is open internationally, with applicants considered regardless of their country of origin, prior work experience or ethnic background. However, candidates must meet the relevant admission requirements of their chosen university and PhD programme.

Applicants should remember that the fellowship application and university admission application are connected but separate steps. Completing the initial HKPFS application alone is not sufficient; applicants must also submit their full PhD applications to their selected universities before the universities’ individual deadlines.

The application window for the 2027/28 intake opened on 1 September 2026, and the deadline is 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time. Late initial applications will not be considered.

For students with strong academic records, research potential, communication skills and leadership abilities, the HKPFS offers an opportunity to pursue advanced doctoral research in Hong Kong while receiving substantial financial fellowship support.

For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the IOM Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme 2026, a three-month reporting initiative designed to support original, accurate, evidence-based and ethically produced journalism about migration in Chiang Rai and surrounding areas of northern Thailand.

Organized by the International Organization for Migration in Thailand, the programme will select five fellows, each of whom will receive a USD 1,000 reporting grant alongside professional mentorship, editorial guidance, programme check-ins, a field visit and potential publication through IOM platforms.

The fellowship will run from 1 October to 31 December 2026, while completed stories must be submitted by 8 January 2027. Applications must be submitted no later than 22 September 2026. The official announcement does not specify a closing time, so candidates should avoid waiting until the final day. Review the official IOM Thailand announcement.

About the Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme

Migration is an important part of Thailand’s social, economic and demographic landscape. Its significance is particularly visible in Chiang Rai, a northern border province where communities, economies and personal experiences are closely connected to cross-border mobility.

Despite the importance of migration, public discussion can sometimes be shaped by incomplete information, stereotypes, sensational reporting or narratives that fail to reflect the realities and contributions of migrants. Journalism plays a significant role in determining how migration is understood by communities, institutions and policymakers.

The Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme seeks to strengthen the ability of local journalists and emerging media practitioners to produce reporting that is:

  • Accurate and based on credible evidence.
  • Balanced in its treatment of complex migration issues.
  • Sensitive to the dignity, safety and rights of migrants.
  • Connected to the realities of Chiang Rai and surrounding areas.
  • Constructive in how it contributes to public understanding.
  • Professionally and ethically produced.
  • Capable of challenging stereotypes and misleading migration narratives.

The programme’s central theme is the reframing of migration narratives and public perceptions to encourage greater inclusion of migrants. Through well-researched stories grounded in evidence, local realities and migrants’ experiences, fellows are expected to help build a more informed and constructive understanding of migration at the local level. Read the official call for proposals.

The initiative is made possible through financial support from the Government of Japan. See the programme announcement from IOM Thailand.

Main Objectives of the Programme

The fellowship is intended to move beyond short-term awareness raising by providing selected participants with practical support to research, produce and complete substantial migration stories.

Its main objectives include:

  1. Supporting local migration journalism

    The programme provides financial and professional assistance for reporting on migration issues connected to Chiang Rai and nearby areas.

  2. Improving the accuracy of migration reporting

    Fellows will be encouraged to use reliable evidence, appropriate sources and properly verified information when developing their stories.

  3. Promoting balanced and ethical storytelling

    The programme emphasizes journalism that avoids harmful stereotypes, respects the dignity of migrants and accurately represents complex migration experiences.

  4. Connecting national migration issues with local realities

    Proposed stories should be relevant to Chiang Rai or its surrounding areas rather than addressing migration only as a broad or abstract international issue.

  5. Strengthening the practical capacity of journalists and emerging storytellers

    Through mentorship, editorial guidance, orientation sessions and programme check-ins, fellows will receive structured support throughout the reporting process.

  6. Expanding public access to evidence-based migration stories

    Completed work may be published through IOM platforms, giving selected fellows an opportunity to reach wider audiences.

What Selected Fellows Will Receive

1. USD 1,000 Reporting Grant

Each of the five selected fellows will receive a reporting grant of USD 1,000 to support the production of an original migration story.

The grant is intended to assist with the reporting and production process. Applicants should therefore present a story idea that is realistic, properly planned and achievable within the available funding and programme period.

This is a reporting grant rather than a salary, academic scholarship or general cash award. It is connected to the successful production of the proposed journalism project. See IOM Thailand’s official fellowship information.

2. Professional Mentorship

Selected fellows will receive mentorship while developing their stories. This support can help participants strengthen their research plans, refine their angles, address gaps in evidence and improve the overall quality of their reporting.

Mentorship is especially valuable for participants working on sensitive migration topics that require careful consideration of informed consent, confidentiality, source protection, representation and the potential consequences of publication.

3. Editorial Guidance

IOM and designated mentors will provide editorial feedback during the reporting process.

Fellows will be expected to respond constructively to this guidance and incorporate relevant recommendations into their work. Editorial support may help participants improve the structure, clarity, factual accuracy, balance and ethical quality of their final stories.

4. Online Orientation and Monthly Check-Ins

Selected participants will take part in an online orientation session at the beginning of the programme.

IOM will also organize monthly check-ins throughout the fellowship period. These sessions are intended to monitor progress, provide guidance, identify emerging challenges and help fellows remain on schedule.

5. Field Visit in Chiang Rai

The programme includes a field visit within Chiang Rai organized by IOM.

The field visit is designed to deepen participants’ understanding of migration dynamics in the province. It will also provide opportunities to exchange experiences with foreign correspondents and other relevant stakeholders. Consult the official call for the participation requirements.

6. Opportunity for Publication

Fellows may have their completed stories published through IOM platforms.

Publication can increase the visibility of the participant’s work while contributing to broader public understanding of migration. It may also strengthen the fellow’s professional portfolio and demonstrate an ability to produce responsible, evidence-based reporting on a complex social issue.

Publication is not automatic or unconditional. Materials developed through the programme will be reviewed by IOM before they are published or otherwise disseminated.

Expected Journalism Project

Applicants must propose an original and feasible story related to migration in Chiang Rai and/or surrounding areas.

A strong project should establish a clear connection between the proposed subject and the local migration context. The idea should be narrow enough to investigate properly within the programme period but significant enough to contribute meaningfully to public understanding.

The proposed story should ultimately demonstrate:

  • A clearly defined migration issue or reporting question.
  • Relevance to Chiang Rai or surrounding communities.
  • A practical reporting and production plan.
  • Credible sources and evidence.
  • Appropriate inclusion of migrant experiences and perspectives.
  • Balanced treatment of the people and institutions involved.
  • Ethical interviewing and reporting practices.
  • Realistic completion within the three-month fellowship.
  • Responsiveness to editorial feedback.
  • Compliance with the final format and supporting-material requirements established by IOM.

Applicants should avoid submitting broad proposals that attempt to cover every dimension of migration. A focused story with identifiable sources, a clear audience and a realistic reporting plan is more likely to be completed effectively.

Responsibilities of Selected Fellows

Receiving the grant carries clear professional and programme obligations. Successful applicants will be expected to:

  1. Produce a high-quality migration story by the agreed deadline.
  2. Participate in the programme’s online orientation.
  3. Attend monthly check-ins organized by IOM.
  4. Participate in the IOM-organized field visit in Chiang Rai.
  5. Remain engaged throughout the fellowship period.
  6. Incorporate appropriate editorial guidance from IOM or designated mentors.
  7. Complete the proposed story within the approved timeline.
  8. Follow applicable professional and ethical journalism standards.
  9. Submit all required supporting materials with the final story.
  10. Ensure that the completed work meets the minimum format requirements stated in the programme documents.
  11. Submit the final story by 8 January 2027.

All materials produced through the programme will be subject to IOM review and approval before publication or dissemination. This review is intended to confirm that funded stories remain within the approved scope, meet ethical and professional standards and comply with relevant IOM requirements. Read the official terms in the call for proposals.

Documents Required for the Application

Applicants should prepare the complete application package before opening the online submission form.

The required materials include:

1. Updated Resume or CV

The resume or CV should clearly present the applicant’s education, journalism or media experience, relevant training, publications, reporting interests and other experience connected to migration, social issues or public-interest communication.

2. Cover Letter

Applicants must provide a cover letter explaining:

  • Their motivation for applying.
  • Their interest in ethical migration journalism.
  • Their proposed story idea.
  • Why the subject is relevant to Chiang Rai or surrounding areas.
  • How they intend to complete the project.

The cover letter and proposed story description should be concise and should not exceed one page.

3. Completed Story Proposal Form

Candidates must download and complete the official Story Proposal Form available through the programme webpage.

The proposal should be internally consistent with the information provided in the cover letter and online application form.

4. Certificate of Relevant IOM Training

Applicants must provide evidence that they completed the qualifying IOM training or e-learning route.

For the e-learning route, both the Migration Explained and Reporting Migration in Thailand modules must be completed.

5. Previous Work Samples

Journalist applicants must provide two relevant samples of previous work.

This requirement is specifically identified for journalist applicants. The samples should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to research, structure and communicate a story professionally. Whenever possible, applicants should select work relevant to migration, human rights, border communities, social inclusion or another complex public-interest issue. Confirm the complete application requirements on the official IOM page.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should follow these steps:

  1. Review the official programme announcement and call for proposals.
  2. Confirm that all location and training requirements are met.
  3. Develop an original and feasible migration story connected to Chiang Rai or surrounding areas.
  4. Update the resume or CV.
  5. Prepare a focused cover letter of no more than one page.
  6. Download and complete the official Story Proposal Form.
  7. Obtain the certificate showing completion of the required training or e-learning modules.
  8. Prepare two relevant work samples if applying as a journalist.
  9. Complete the online application form available through the official IOM Thailand programme page.
  10. Submit the entire application no later than 22 September 2026.

Apply through the official IOM Thailand opportunity page

Candidates should carefully check uploaded documents before submitting. The story title, subject, proposed activities and timeline should remain consistent across the cover letter, proposal form and online application.

Important Programme Dates

Programme stage Date
Applications opened 1 September 2026
Application deadline 22 September 2026
Shortlisting and interviews 23–25 September 2026
Selection announcement 29 September 2026
Fellowship period 1 October–31 December 2026
Final story submission 8 January 2027

The short period between the application deadline and interviews means applicants should remain available and regularly monitor the email address and telephone number provided in their application.

How to Prepare a Strong Story Proposal

Although applicants should follow the official Story Proposal Form, the following practical steps can help produce a clearer and more competitive submission.

Define a Focused Local Issue

Identify a specific migration-related issue that can be examined within Chiang Rai or nearby areas. Avoid a subject that is too broad to research properly within three months.

Explain Why the Story Matters

Clearly describe why the proposed story is relevant to local communities and how it could improve public understanding of migration.

Present a Credible Reporting Plan

Explain which people, communities, experts, institutions, documents and other sources may be consulted. Applicants should demonstrate that the proposed reporting process is realistic.

Center Accuracy and Ethics

The proposal should explain how information will be verified and how the dignity, privacy and safety of migrants or other potentially vulnerable sources will be protected.

Include Migrant Perspectives Responsibly

Migration stories should not treat migrants only as statistics or passive subjects. Where appropriate and safe, the proposal should create space for migrants to explain their experiences in their own words.

Demonstrate Feasibility

The reporting scope, production method and expected output should be achievable between October and December 2026 and within the USD 1,000 grant.

Prepare for Editorial Collaboration

Applicants should demonstrate openness to mentorship, review and constructive editorial feedback. The fellowship is structured as a supported reporting process rather than an unrestricted financial award.

Review Every Document for Consistency

The CV, cover letter, proposal form, work samples and online application should support the same professional narrative. Conflicting titles, timelines or project descriptions could weaken the application.

Contact for Questions

Questions about the programme or application process may be directed to:

Email: mediathailand@iom.int

Applicants should first review the official announcement and call for proposals before contacting IOM. Questions should be clear, specific and directly related to information not already addressed in the published materials.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

22 September 2026

No specific closing time or time zone is stated in the accessible programme announcement. Applicants should submit early to avoid technical problems or uncertainty on the final day.

Conclusion

The IOM Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme 2026 offers an important opportunity to transform a strong local story idea into professionally supported, evidence-based journalism.

Five selected fellows will receive USD 1,000 each, along with mentorship, editorial guidance, structured check-ins, a field visit in Chiang Rai and potential publication through IOM platforms. More importantly, participants will contribute to a wider effort to improve how migration is reported and understood in northern Thailand.

This is a project-based programme with meaningful responsibilities. A successful fellow must be prepared to conduct careful research, engage ethically with sources, respond to editorial feedback and submit a completed story by 8 January 2027.

Interested candidates should prepare their application documents carefully and submit the online form by 22 September 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Manchester Metropolitan University (Manchester Met) is providing a range of fellowship opportunities designed to support researchers at different stages of their academic careers. The university’s fellowship portfolio includes schemes covering areas such as early-career research, engineering, science and technology, artificial intelligence, humanities and social sciences, biological sciences, and interdisciplinary research.

Manchester Met states that it is committed to the development of early-career researchers and supports outstanding candidates seeking externally funded research opportunities. Its fellowship portfolio includes both opportunities currently open for applications or expressions of interest and previously advertised schemes.

For applicants interested in pursuing an academic research career in the United Kingdom, the university’s fellowship opportunities provide potential routes to develop independent research, strengthen research records, build collaborations and progress toward longer-term academic careers.

About Manchester Metropolitan University’s Fellowship Opportunities

Manchester Metropolitan University is based in Manchester, United Kingdom, and has established a broad research environment focused on innovation, knowledge exchange and societal impact.

The university describes its research as being driven by a desire to make an impact on the world, building on its position in Manchester while pursuing national and global impact. It also highlights its facilities, research activities and academic environment as important elements of its research offering.

Its fellowship opportunities are particularly relevant to researchers looking for structured support to develop their research careers and pursue externally funded schemes.

The university’s fellowship page currently highlights several schemes, including:

  1. Leverhulme Trust Early Career Fellowships
  2. STFC Ernest Rutherford Fellowships
  3. Royal Academy of Engineering Research Fellowships
  4. UKRI Future Leaders Fellowships
  5. UKRI Turing AI Pioneer Interdisciplinary Fellowship
  6. British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowships
  7. Marie Skłodowska-Curie Action Postdoctoral Fellowships
  8. Leverhulme Trust Research Leadership Awards
  9. BBSRC Fellowships
  10. The Sir Robert Boyd Fellowship
  11. Third Century Fellowship Scheme

However, applicants should carefully check the status of each scheme because the page contains both currently open and closed opportunities.

Featured Current Opportunity: Leverhulme Trust Early Career Fellowship

Among the opportunities listed by Manchester Met, the Leverhulme Trust Early Career Fellowship is identified as having Expressions of Interest now open.

The scheme is intended for early-career researchers who already have a research record but have not yet held a full-time permanent academic post. The fellowship enables successful researchers to undertake a significant piece of publishable research.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to researchers who are building their academic careers and want dedicated time and institutional support to develop a substantial research project.

How the Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship Works

The scheme operates through a joint-support model.

Under this arrangement:

  • The Leverhulme Trust contributes part of the total salary cost.
  • Manchester Metropolitan University provides the remaining salary cost as match funding.
  • Because there is a limit to the number of proposals that can be supported, Manchester Met conducts an internal selection process.
  • Applicants need support from a prospective host School or Department.
  • Researchers interested in applying should contact the relevant School or Department Research contact to discuss the potential for Manchester Met to host their proposed research and receive support with the Expression of Interest form.

This means prospective applicants should not treat the process as a straightforward direct application to the external funder. Manchester Met first conducts an internal selection process before selected candidates proceed to the external fellowship application.

Key Deadline for the Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship

The current Manchester Met Expression of Interest deadline is

Friday, 9 October 2026

Applicants are required to submit their Expressions of Interest to the relevant School or Department contact by this date.

Following submission, the Schools and Departments will nominate their selected candidates for internal review.

The internal selection panel is scheduled to meet on:

5 November 2026

Manchester Met expects to select up to two applications to progress to submission to the Leverhulme Trust.

Successful candidates will then be notified following the internal panel and supported by a mentor and the Research Development Team as they prepare for external submission.

The external submission is scheduled for:

18 February 2027

Who Is the Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship For?

The fellowship is specifically designed for early-career researchers who have an established research record but have not yet held a full-time permanent academic position.

The purpose is to enable these researchers to undertake a significant piece of publishable research. The scheme is intended to support researchers at a relatively early point in their academic careers and may help position them for a future permanent academic role.

The fellowships are tenable for three years.

Research and Career Development Through the Fellowship

The Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship is structured around the development of independent research.

Rather than simply providing short-term research support, the scheme is intended to give an early-career researcher the opportunity to undertake a substantial project capable of producing significant publishable work.

The fellowship may therefore be valuable for researchers seeking to:

  • Develop an independent research profile.
  • Complete a substantial research project.
  • Produce publishable research.
  • Strengthen their academic track record.
  • Develop their position within their research field.
  • Work toward a longer-term academic career.
  • Establish connections with a UK university research environment.
  • Benefit from institutional mentoring and research development support.

Manchester Met notes that the fellowship is intended to assist researchers at a relatively early stage of their academic careers and expresses the hope that the appointment can lead to a more permanent position for the individual, either at the same university or elsewhere.

Important Consideration for Prospective Applicants

Researchers considering the Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship should understand the distinction between the Manchester Met Expression of Interest stage and the external Leverhulme Trust application.

The Manchester Met process involves:

  1. Identifying a suitable Manchester Met School or Department.
  2. Discussing the research proposal and potential hosting arrangements with the relevant research contact.
  3. Preparing and submitting the Expression of Interest.
  4. Participating in Manchester Met’s internal selection process.
  5. If selected, receiving institutional support to develop the external application.
  6. Preparing for submission to the Leverhulme Trust by the external deadline.

Because Manchester Met states that there is a limit on the number of proposals it can support, applicants should carefully engage with the relevant School or Department before submitting their EOI.

Other Fellowship Opportunities at Manchester Metropolitan University

Manchester Met’s fellowship portfolio extends beyond the Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship.

STFC Ernest Rutherford Fellowships

The STFC Ernest Rutherford Fellowships support outstanding early-career researchers seeking to establish independent research careers within the Science and Technology Facilities Council’s core science programme.

Manchester Met’s page identifies the 2026 opportunity as open and invites potential applicants to submit an Expression of Interest to the university.

For that round, the stated Manchester Met EOI deadline was 17 July 2026.

Applicants should note that this deadline has already passed.

Royal Academy of Engineering Research Fellowships

The Royal Academy of Engineering Research Fellowships are designed for outstanding early-career researchers who want to develop into future research leaders in engineering.

Manchester Met invited prospective applicants to submit Expressions of Interest for this scheme, but the university page states that the call is now closed.

The stated EOI deadline was 25 May 2026.

UKRI Future Leaders Fellowships

The UKRI Future Leaders Fellowships support researchers seeking to develop their research careers.

Manchester Met’s page states that the Round 11 call for Expressions of Interest was closed. The university had anticipated the next round and invited researchers, including external candidates, to participate in its internal process.

Research projects in any area could be considered where they aligned with the current research focus or expertise of the relevant faculty.

An important point is that the university’s internal EOI is not itself an offer of a fellowship position. Employment would only become available if the proposal were ultimately funded by UKRI.

Marie Skłodowska-Curie Action Postdoctoral Fellowships

The Marie Skłodowska-Curie Action (MSCA) Postdoctoral Fellowships support excellent researchers at an early stage of their careers to undertake a fellowship in another country.

Manchester Met invited Expressions of Interest from prospective applicants seeking to join its 2026 MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship cohort.

Selected candidates would receive a detailed programme of support to prepare their applications for the MSCA call. The university stated that applicants did not need to have identified a supervisor in advance, although they could indicate one if already identified.

For the referenced 2026 internal process, the EOI deadline was 16 February 2026, meaning that particular call is now closed.

UKRI Turing AI Pioneer Interdisciplinary Fellowship

The UKRI Turing AI Pioneer Interdisciplinary Fellowship is aimed at established researchers across the UKRI remit who do not have a background in core artificial intelligence research.

The opportunity is designed for researchers who want to:

  • Build domain-relevant AI capability.
  • Develop advanced AI approaches.
  • Apply AI approaches to a specific research challenge in their chosen field.
  • Work across disciplinary boundaries.

The Manchester Met page currently identifies this opportunity as closed.

British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowships

The British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowships are designed for early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences.

The fellowship supports researchers who want to pursue an independent research project leading toward completion of a significant piece of publishable research.

The Manchester Met page currently identifies this opportunity as closed.

Leverhulme Trust Research Leadership Awards

The Leverhulme Trust Research Leadership Awards are intended for talented scholars embarking on a university career who need to develop a research team capable of tackling a distinctive research problem.

Manchester Met’s page states that external applicants whose research fits within particular university departments and schools could express interest in the opportunity.

The listed areas include:

  • Department of English
  • Department of Sociology
  • School of Digital Arts
  • Strategy, Enterprise and Sustainability
  • School of Computing and Maths
  • School of Engineering and Environment
  • School of Biological and Chemical Sciences
  • School of Sports and Exercise Sciences

However, the page states that this opportunity is closed and also clarifies that the particular opportunity described on the page was not itself a fellowship.

BBSRC Fellowships Scheme

The BBSRC Fellowships Scheme supports research in biotechnology and biological sciences.

The Manchester Met page describes research projects involving areas such as:

  • Plants
  • Microbes
  • Animals
  • Humans
  • Tools and technologies underpinning biological research

The referenced Manchester Met call invited Expressions of Interest as the first stage of an internal process. It was not itself an offer of a fellowship position from the university.

The page identifies the referenced call as closed, with its EOI deadline having been 14 March 2024.

The Sir Robert Boyd Fellowship

The Dowager Countess Eleanor Peel Trust (DCEPT) Sir Robert Boyd Fellowship was another fellowship opportunity featured on the Manchester Met page.

The university noted that only one application was allowed from each university and therefore conducted an internal Expression of Interest process.

The referenced 2024 EOI deadline was 26 August 2024, and the page currently identifies the opportunity as closed.

Third Century Fellowship Scheme

The Third Century Fellowship Scheme was launched by Manchester Metropolitan University in connection with its 200th anniversary in 2024.

The fellowship was aimed at exceptional researchers in the early stages of their postdoctoral careers who wanted to establish themselves in their field through independent research.

The university described the target candidates as emerging research leaders with significant experience and a notable record of research outputs.

The opportunity is currently listed as closed.

Who Qualifies for These Opportunities?

Because Manchester Met’s fellowship page contains several different schemes, eligibility varies from one fellowship to another.

For the currently highlighted Leverhulme Trust Early Career Fellowship, the stated target group is:

  • Early-career researchers.
  • Researchers who already have a research record.
  • Researchers who have not yet held a full-time permanent academic post.
  • Researchers seeking to undertake a significant piece of publishable research.
  • Researchers who can secure the support of a prospective Manchester Met host School or Department.

The source provided does not state a specific nationality, race or continental restriction for the Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship on the page excerpt. Therefore, applicants should consult the official Leverhulme Trust guidance for the complete external eligibility requirements before applying.

For the other fellowships, eligibility is scheme-specific. For example, the British Academy fellowship focuses on humanities and social sciences, the Royal Academy of Engineering fellowship focuses on engineering, and the BBSRC scheme focuses on biotechnology and biological sciences.

Application Process for the Current Manchester Met Opportunity

Researchers interested in the currently open Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship should approach the application strategically.

Step 1: Identify a suitable research area

Applicants should have a strong research project capable of producing a significant piece of publishable work.

Step 2: Identify a potential Manchester Met host

The applicant should identify the School or Department at Manchester Met that is most appropriate for the proposed research.

Step 3: Contact the relevant research representative

The university specifically asks applicants to contact the relevant School or Department Research contact to discuss the possibility of being hosted and to receive support with the EOI process.

Step 4: Submit the Expression of Interest

The EOI must be submitted to the relevant School or Department contact by:

9 October 2026

Step 5: Internal selection

Manchester Met’s internal selection panel will review nominations on:

5 November 2026

Up to two applications are expected to progress to the external submission stage.

Step 6: Develop the external application

Candidates selected through the internal process will receive support from a mentor and the Research Development Team.

Step 7: Submit to the Leverhulme Trust

The supported candidates will work toward the external submission deadline of:

18 February 2027

APPLY HERE

Why Manchester Metropolitan University?

Manchester Metropolitan University presents itself as a major UK university with a strong commitment to research, innovation and societal impact.

The university highlights its:

  • State-of-the-art facilities.
  • Innovative teaching.
  • Research strengths.
  • Knowledge exchange activities.
  • Commitment to innovation and progress.
  • National and global research impact.
  • Interdisciplinary research environment.

Manchester Met also states that its research seeks to transform lives by harnessing creativity and confidence to deliver societal impact.

For researchers, this environment can provide an opportunity to connect independent research with broader academic, institutional and societal challenges.

Important Dates at a Glance

For the currently open Leverhulme Trust Early Career Fellowship process:

Stage Date
Manchester Met EOI deadline 9 October 2026
Internal selection panel 5 November 2026
Up to two applications selected Following internal panel
External application support Following internal selection
Leverhulme Trust external submission 18 February 2027
Fellowship duration 3 years

The dates above relate specifically to the current Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship process described on the Manchester Met page.

Visit HERE for more information about the Manchester Metropolitan University Fellowship Opportunities 2026–2027.

Conclusion

Manchester Metropolitan University’s fellowship portfolio provides researchers with access to a range of research funding and career-development pathways across numerous academic disciplines.

The Leverhulme Trust Early Career Fellowship is the key opportunity on the supplied page currently identified as open for Expressions of Interest. It is particularly relevant to early-career researchers who have already developed a research record but have not yet held a full-time permanent academic position and who want to undertake a significant piece of publishable research.

The Manchester Met process is competitive and involves an internal selection stage before candidates can progress to the external Leverhulme Trust application. Prospective applicants should therefore begin by identifying an appropriate Manchester Met School or Department and engaging with the relevant research contact.

The immediate deadline for the current Manchester Met Expression of Interest is 9 October 2026, followed by internal selection on 5 November 2026. Up to two applications will be selected to proceed toward the external submission, with institutional mentoring and Research Development Team support provided to successful internal candidates. The external submission is scheduled for 18 February 2027.

Researchers should also note that the Manchester Met fellowship page contains several other schemes whose calls are already closed. Therefore, candidates should always verify the current status, eligibility requirements and deadlines of a particular fellowship before preparing an application.

For more global Fellowship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is inviting applications for a Category II Internship within its Composite Indicator Research Section, Department for Economics and Data Analytics (DEDA), under the IP and Innovation Ecosystems Sector (IES).

This six-month internship will be based at WIPO Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, and is designed for qualified candidates with an academic background in economics, data science or a related field who have strong interests in statistical analysis, econometrics, data visualization, innovation economics and policy research.

The selected intern will contribute to major WIPO research publications, including the Global Innovation Index (GII) 2027 and the World Intangible Investment Highlights (WIIH) 2027.

The internship is expected to begin on January 4, 2027, and provides a monthly stipend of CHF 2,170, together with medical insurance, annual leave and sick leave benefits.

The application deadline is September 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM CEST.

About the WIPO Internship Program

The WIPO Internship Program is designed to help students and recent graduates complement their academic education with practical professional experience in an international organisation.

Through participation in the workplace, interns can apply their academic knowledge to real-world projects while developing professional skills and competencies.

The programme also provides opportunities for learning through:

  • Practical work experience.
  • Exposure to an international working environment.
  • Supervision and feedback from experienced colleagues.
  • Technical mentoring.
  • Structured courses and learning programmes where available.
  • Experience working within the United Nations common system.

For candidates interested in international organisations, economics, innovation, data analytics and public policy, this internship provides an opportunity to gain practical experience while working on internationally relevant research and publications.

About the Host Department

This internship is hosted by the Composite Indicator Research Section within the Department for Economics and Data Analytics (DEDA) of WIPO’s IP and Innovation Ecosystems Sector (IES).

The intern will work under the supervision of the Head of the Composite Indicator Research Section.

The section’s work involves economic and data analysis, including research associated with innovation and intangible investment.

The internship therefore combines several areas, including:

  • Economics
  • Statistics
  • Data analytics
  • Econometrics
  • Innovation research
  • Economic publications
  • Data visualization
  • Policy research
  • Digital communications

Main Objectives of the Internship

The internship has several key objectives.

APPLY HERE

Apply Academic Knowledge

The intern will have an opportunity to apply knowledge of economics, statistics and data analytics to practical work involving economic publications and policymaking.

This means the internship is not purely administrative. Candidates will be expected to contribute analytical skills to research and publication-related activities.

Receive Technical Supervision and Mentoring

The intern will work under the guidance of experienced WIPO staff.

This provides an opportunity to receive technical supervision and mentoring while developing practical research and analytical skills.

Gain United Nations System Experience

The internship provides experience working within a United Nations common system organization.

This can give successful candidates exposure to the working environment, processes and professional standards of an international organisation.

Key Research Projects

The successful intern will contribute to work associated with two major publications.

Global Innovation Index 2027

One of the primary areas of work will be the Global Innovation Index (GII) 2027.

The Global Innovation Index is associated with research and analysis concerning innovation performance.

The intern may contribute analytical inputs and other research-related activities supporting the preparation of the 2027 edition.

This can provide practical experience in using data and economic analysis to support an internationally recognised research publication.

World Intangible Investment Highlights 2027

The intern will also contribute to the World Intangible Investment Highlights (WIIH) 2027.

This work focuses on measuring investment in intangible assets and communicating findings through research publications and related materials.

The combination of the GII and WIIH projects means that the intern can gain exposure to economic research, data analysis, innovation and intangible investment.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Head of the Composite Indicator Research Section, the intern will contribute to several areas of work.

1. Research and Analytical Contributions

The intern will provide analytical inputs to the production of:

  • Global Innovation Index 2027.
  • World Intangible Investment Highlights 2027.

This may involve working with economic and statistical information and supporting research used in the preparation of the publications.

2. Data Visualization

The intern will provide support for data visualization.

This is particularly relevant for candidates interested in communicating complex datasets and economic findings through clear and accessible visual formats.

Applicants with experience using modern data visualization tools may therefore have an advantage.

3. Social Media and Website Content

The intern will also support the preparation of content for:

  • WIPO’s social media platforms.
  • The WIPO website.

This work will be carried out under editorial guidance.

Candidates with experience creating digital content, drafting web content or preparing social media materials may therefore find this aspect of the internship particularly relevant.

4. Event Organisation

The intern will assist with the organisation of events connected to the two major publications.

Responsibilities may include preparing:

  • Presentations.
  • Talking points.
  • Background materials.
  • Other event-related documentation.

This provides exposure to the communication and event-management side of international research projects.

5. Logistical and Administrative Support

The intern may also perform other related tasks as required.

Examples include:

  • Drafting invitations.
  • Coordinating event logistics.
  • Supporting administrative processes.
  • Providing general logistical assistance related to research activities and events.

The internship therefore combines analytical, communication, research and organisational responsibilities.

Educational Requirements

The essential educational requirement is an:

Advanced university degree (master’s degree) in economics, data science or a related field.

Candidates should therefore have an appropriate postgraduate academic background relevant to the work of the Composite Indicator Research Section.

Relevant academic areas may include economics, data science and related disciplines where the candidate has developed strong quantitative, analytical or research capabilities.

Statistical and Programming Experience

Applicants must have experience using specialised software and programming languages for statistical or econometric analysis.

The announcement specifically highlights:

  • R
  • Python

Experience with either R, Python or both is therefore particularly relevant to the position.

Candidates should be able to demonstrate practical experience using these tools for statistical analysis, econometric work, data processing or related research activities.

Data Visualization Skills

Familiarity with modern data visualization tools is an essential requirement.

Applicants should also have an interest in developing their data visualization skills further.

This suggests that candidates should be comfortable working with data and interested in transforming analytical findings into understandable visual outputs.

Desirable Skills and Experience

Several additional qualifications are listed as desirable rather than essential.

These include:

Applied Economics

Knowledge of or experience with applied economics is an advantage.

Candidates with experience applying economic concepts and analytical methods to real-world economic questions may therefore be particularly well suited.

Innovation Economics

Experience or knowledge of innovation economics is also desirable.

This is particularly relevant given the internship’s connection to the Global Innovation Index and WIPO’s broader work on innovation ecosystems.

Social Media and Web Content

Experience drafting content for social media and web use is another advantage.

Candidates who can combine technical research skills with strong digital communication abilities may therefore be able to contribute across several areas of the internship.

Communication Skills

The position also values:

  • Strong oral communication.
  • Strong written communication.
  • Strong interpersonal skills.

The ability to communicate effectively is important because the intern will contribute to research publications, digital content, presentations and events.

Multicultural Working Environment

Candidates should have the ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment.

Because WIPO is an international organisation, interns are expected to work respectfully and effectively with colleagues from different professional, cultural and national backgrounds.

Professional Integrity

Sound judgement and integrity are also listed among the desirable competencies.

Language Requirements

Excellent written and spoken English is an essential requirement.

Candidates must therefore be able to communicate effectively in English in both professional and written settings.

Knowledge of other official United Nations languages is desirable.

Additional UN languages may therefore strengthen an applicant’s profile, although they are not listed as essential.

Organisational Competencies

WIPO identifies several organisational competencies relevant to the internship.

Candidates should demonstrate the ability to:

  1. Communicate effectively
  2. Show team spirit
  3. Demonstrate integrity
  4. Value diversity
  5. Produce results
  6. Show service orientation
  7. See the big picture
  8. Seek change and innovation
  9. Develop yourself and others

These competencies reflect the professional behaviours expected within the organisation.

Internship Duration

The internship has an expected duration of:

Six months

The internship may be renewed, subject to the applicable conditions.

The minimum duration is six months, while the maximum total duration is 12 months.

Expected Start Date

The expected start date is:

January 4, 2027

Candidates should therefore be prepared to undertake the internship from this date if selected.

Location and Remote Work

The internship will take place at:

WIPO Headquarters, Geneva, Switzerland

The selected candidate will therefore need to work physically from WIPO’s headquarters in Geneva.

Internship Working Hours

The stipend stated in the vacancy is based on a full-time internship of 40 hours per week.

Candidates should therefore be prepared to commit to a full-time schedule for the duration of the internship.

Stipend and Benefits

The selected intern will receive a monthly stipend of:

CHF 2,170

Option B: Individuals Pursuing a Subsequent Degree

Individuals who have already obtained their first advanced university degree and are currently pursuing a subsequent university degree may also qualify.

Option C: Recent Advanced Degree Graduates

Individuals who obtained their most recent advanced university degree less than two years before the date of their internship application may also qualify.

Applicants should carefully determine which of these three categories applies to their situation before applying.

Who Should Apply?

The internship is particularly suited to candidates who combine postgraduate academic training with practical quantitative and analytical skills.

A competitive candidate would ideally have:

  • A master’s degree or qualifying advanced university degree in economics, data science or a related field.
  • Experience with R and/or Python.
  • Experience in statistical or econometric analysis.
  • Familiarity with modern data visualization tools.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • An interest in economics, innovation, data analytics and policy research.
  • Strong communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal skills.
  • The ability to work in a multicultural environment.

Additional experience in applied economics, innovation economics, social media, web content and data communication would be advantageous.

Application Requirements

1. Motivation Letter

The motivation letter should explain the candidate’s interest in the internship and demonstrate their suitability for the position.

Candidates should use the letter to connect their academic background, technical skills and professional interests with the work of the Composite Indicator Research Section.

2. Curriculum Vitae

The CV should clearly present relevant:

  • Educational qualifications.

Important LinkedIn Application Requirement

The CV and cover letter must be combined into one single PDF file when submitting through LinkedIn Easy Apply.

Applicants should not upload them as separate documents if using the Easy Apply route.

Most importantly, applications that do not include both a motivation letter and a curriculum vitae will not be considered.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

September 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM CEST

Candidates should ensure that all required application materials are submitted before the deadline.

Because applications missing either the motivation letter or CV will not be considered, applicants should verify their submission carefully before sending it.

Application Process

Interested candidates should:

  1. Review the eligibility requirements for Category II internships.

  3. Prepare a motivation letter.
  4. Prepare an up-to-date CV.

Why This WIPO Internship Is Valuable

This internship provides an opportunity to gain practical experience at an international organisation while working on research and publications related to innovation, economics and data.

The successful intern will gain exposure to several professional areas, including:

  • Economic research.
  • Statistical analysis.
  • Econometric programming.
  • Data visualization.
  • Innovation research.
  • Intangible investment research.
  • Economic publications.
  • International policy work.
  • Digital communication.
  • Event preparation.
  • Working within a multicultural international organisation.

The opportunity can therefore be particularly valuable for candidates looking to combine economics or data science with international development, innovation policy and research.

Important Points to Remember

  • The internship is based in Geneva, Switzerland.

Conclusion

The WIPO Economics and Data Analytics Internship 2027 offers an excellent opportunity for qualified postgraduate students and recent advanced-degree graduates to gain practical experience in economics, statistics, data analytics, innovation research and international policymaking.

Based at WIPO Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, the six-month internship will allow the selected candidate to contribute to major publications such as the Global Innovation Index 2027 and World Intangible Investment Highlights 2027.

Additional experience in applied economics, innovation economics, social media and web content can further strengthen an application.
